hero.title: Invoicing for Czech and Slovak businesses, without the paperwork
hero.subtitle: Issue invoices by voice over Telegram or WhatsApp, export them to ISDOC, and stay confident everything matches ARES and current regulations.

features.title: Everything you need to invoice, in one place

isdoc.title: ISDOC export
isdoc.description: Invoices in ISDOC format, ready for your accountant and the tax authorities – no manual re-entry.

aiVoice.title: Invoice from a voice message
aiVoice.description: Dictate an invoice over Telegram or WhatsApp and let AI prepare a draft for a quick review.

compliance.title: Mandatory details check
compliance.description: Before you issue an invoice we check it has everything Czech or Slovak VAT and commercial law requires – company ID, VAT number, addresses, line items. Customer details come from ARES.

multilang.title: Czech, Slovak, and English
multilang.description: The whole app and your invoices work in three languages from day one.

qr.title: A QR payment code on every invoice
qr.description: Every invoice carries a QR code in the Czech Banking Association standard. Add your account number or IBAN and your customer just scans and pays.

bankSync.title: Bank and PayPal payments match themselves
bankSync.description: Connect Fio, another bank over PSD2 or PayPal, and Billanta downloads incoming payments and marks invoices paid, with the PayPal fee included.

reminders.title: Overdue reminders
reminders.description: Billanta watches unpaid invoices and sends the customer a reminder with the invoice link and QR payment.

vat.title: VAT return for EPO
vat.description: From invoices and expenses we prepare the XML VAT return and control statement for the Czech tax portal.

expenses.title: Receipts from a photo
expenses.description: Snap a receipt or upload a PDF and AI fills in the supplier, amount, VAT and due date.

recurring.title: Recurring and bulk invoices
recurring.description: Retainers and rent are issued on schedule. From a template you can bill many customers at once.

templates.title: Templates and custom variables
templates.description: Save a document as a template, edit email texts and insert variables like '{number}' or '{due_date}'.

time.title: Time tracking
time.description: A timer and manual logs per project. Turn unbilled work into an invoice at the project's rate in one click.

taxEstimate.title: What you keep
taxEstimate.description: Each invoice shows a rough amount after income tax and insurance under Czech sole-trader rules. For the whole year we work out the tax, insurance and next advances.

currencies.title: Foreign currency invoices
currencies.description: EUR, USD and more. The ČNB rate for the supply date fills in by itself and is converted to CZK for VAT.

clientPortal.title: Client portal
clientPortal.description: One permanent link per client: all their invoices and quotes, what is left to pay and what is overdue.

migration.title: Switch from another app
migration.description: From BitFaktura and Fakturoid straight over the API with the original PDFs, from iDoklad or Excel via CSV. You see a preview before saving.

api.title: API and webhooks
api.description: A REST API with your own keys, webhooks for Slack, Discord or your own system, and a due-date calendar.

team.title: Team, accountant, several companies
team.description: Invite colleagues and your accountant with their own role. Run a sole trade and a company from one account.

auditLog.title: Change history
auditLog.description: Who changed what and when, including changes by AI and over the API. An issued document can only be corrected with a stated reason.

reports.title: Reports by period
reports.description: Revenue, expenses and top customers for a month, quarter or year, compared with the previous period.

backups.title: Backups to your own storage
backups.description: Company data is saved regularly to Google Drive, your server over SFTP or a webhook. Download everything in one click.

capture.title: Dictate or type it
capture.description: A voice note on Telegram or WhatsApp, a photo of a receipt or one sentence. AI fills in the customer from ARES and the items.
capture.highlight: AI on the free plan too

draft.title: Check the draft
draft.description: Billanta checks the required details, VAT and numbering. Nothing is issued until you confirm it.

issue.title: Issue and send
issue.description: A PDF with a QR payment code, ISDOC, and UBL for Slovakia. Your client gets an email with a link to the invoice.

getPaid.title: Payments match themselves
getPaid.description: From Fio, another bank via PSD2 or PayPal. Each invoice shows what you keep after income tax and levies.

finalCta.title: Ready to simplify your invoicing?
finalCta.subtitle: Free to start, no credit card required.

footer.tagline: Modern invoicing for Czech and Slovak businesses.

seo.title: Billanta – online invoicing for Czech and Slovak businesses
seo.description: Issue invoices with ISDOC export, ARES customer lookup and a QR payment code. Dictate a draft as a voice message over Telegram or WhatsApp. Free to start.

free.a: You can start free, with no card, for 10 documents a month. Paid plans start at {price} a month excl. VAT billed yearly; see the pricing page for details.

slovakia.a: Yes. The app is available in Slovak, looks customers up in the Slovak RPO register, puts a PAY by square QR code on invoices and plans are priced in euro. On the Plus plan it prepares the Slovak VAT return, control statement and EC sales list for eDane. It already creates UBL e-invoice files (Peppol BIS 3.0); sending over the Peppol network for the e-invoicing mandate from 2027 is in progress.

isdoc.q: What is ISDOC and why do I need it?
isdoc.a: ISDOC is the Czech electronic invoice standard. Accounting software can import it automatically, so your accountant never has to retype anything.

ares.q: How does the ARES lookup work?
ares.a: Enter a company ID (IČO) and Billanta fetches the customer’s name, address and VAT ID straight from the public ARES registry, so nothing is retyped and no typos creep in.

voice.a: Yes. Send a voice message over Telegram or WhatsApp and AI prepares a draft invoice from it. It only becomes final once you have reviewed and confirmed it yourself.

data.a: Each business’s data is isolated from every other business in the database. You can download a backup at any time, or have it saved automatically to your own storage in settings.

compare.title: Compared with the alternatives
compare.lead: More for free, a lower price and AI on every plan. Next to Fakturoid, iDoklad, SuperFaktura, Vyfakturuj and BitFaktura.
compare.more: Full comparison with Fakturoid, iDoklad and others

psd2.hint: Billanta downloads new incoming payments straight from your bank or PayPal and matches them to invoices by variable symbol and amount. Fio connects with an API token, PayPal with your REST app credentials, other banks over PSD2: you sign in at your bank and grant read-only access to the account (up to 180 days, 90 at many banks). Banks allow only a few unattended reads a day, so PSD2 accounts are synced about every 6 hours. Outgoing payments are not downloaded and nothing can be paid through the connection.

psd2.bankHint: Banks across the EEA supported by our licensed PSD2 provider Enable Banking. Revolut is listed under Lithuania, Wise under Belgium. After Continue you are sent to your online banking to sign in and choose the accounts.
psd2.note: You sign in at your bank directly; Billanta never sees your banking credentials. Withdraw consent at any time by disconnecting the account or in your online banking.

paypal.credentialsHint: In the PayPal Developer Dashboard (developer.paypal.com → Apps & Credentials) create a REST app, enable Transaction search in its features and copy the Client ID and Secret. Billanta only reads received payments with them and sends nothing. They are stored encrypted and never shown again.

paypal.note: Received payments are matched to invoices by the invoice number or variable symbol in the note, and by amount. The fee PayPal kept is booked on the invoice, so reports show the net income too. PayPal publishes transactions with a delay of up to 3 hours.

epo.title: How to file the VAT return, control statement and EC sales list
epo.lead: Upload the XML files above to EPO or send them via your data box. We walk you through the chosen route step by step. Nothing is sent from here.

deadlines.monthlyHint: The VAT return, control statement and EC sales list are due by the 25th of the following month; a weekend or holiday moves it to the next working day.
deadlines.quarterlyHint: Return due by the 25th after the quarter ends. Individuals file the control statement quarterly, companies always monthly.

epo.channelTitle: How do you want to file?
epo.channelHint: Anyone with a data box (every company, sole traders since 2023) must file electronically. Control statements and EC sales lists are always electronic.

ds.name: Via data box
ds.when: Simplest if you have a data box: just attach the XML to a message, no signature needed.
steps: Download the XML above – each filing is a separate file.
We recommend loading it into EPO first (Načtení souboru → Kontrola), filling in the tax office and fixing warnings, then saving it back as XML.
Log in to your data box and write a new message to your tax office (its box ID is in the office list).
Attach one XML file per message.
Send it and keep the delivery receipt.

epo.name: Via EPO
epo.when: The Financial Administration's web form. Submit through your data box (logging in from EPO) or with a qualified electronic signature.
steps: Download the XML above.
Open EPO → Elektronická podání → Načtení souboru and pick the XML.
Check sections D and P: tax office, regional branch and contact details.
Click Kontrola and fix errors; warnings are informational.
Choose Pokračovat v podání → Odeslat přes datovou schránku, or send with an electronic signature.
Keep the filing confirmation (PDF) and the sent XML.

mojeDane.name: MOJE daně portal
mojeDane.when: For individuals with a bank identity or eID card; the filing goes straight from the portal.
steps: Download the XML above.
Log in to the MOJE daně portal with your bank identity or eID.
In EPO choose Načtení souboru and upload the XML.
Check it, fill in the tax office and run Kontrola.
Submit with Podat; the confirmation is in your documents overview.

tips.title: Before you file
items: The data comes from the invoices and expenses issued in Billanta – make sure all documents for the period are entered.
A late control statement means a CZK 1,000 fine; a request from the office must be answered within 5 working days.
File corrections as a supplementary return or follow-up control statement by changing the filing type in EPO.
Not sure? Invite your accountant to the team (Settings → Team) – they see the exports and can file for you.

rate.hint: How amounts in a foreign currency are converted to CZK, separately on the invoice and in your reports. The rate is saved with the document when it is issued and does not change after that.
rate.cnbDailyHint: The ČNB rate valid on the date of taxable supply, as § 38 of the Czech VAT Act requires for VAT. If ČNB published no rate that day, the last earlier one is used. A document with VAT always uses this rate.
rate.noneHint: The document won't show a conversion to CZK. The ČNB rate is still saved for your reports.

rate.reportTitle: In reports and the income tax estimate
rate.reportDailyHint: Each document is converted at the rate saved on it.
rate.annualHint: The uniform rate (jednotný kurz) under § 38(1) of the Czech Income Tax Act. We work it out ourselves as the average of the ČNB rates on the last day of each month, the same way the tax authority (GFŘ) publishes it after the year ends.
rate.invoiceStaysDaily: Invoices still show the daily ČNB rate because VAT law requires it, and the uniform rate is only used in your reports.
rate.computedError: The ČNB rates could not be loaded right now. Reports will use your own rate, otherwise the document's rate.
rate.computedEmpty: No month has ended yet to calculate a rate from.

rate.annualTitle: Your own rate for a year
rate.annualEmpty: You don't need to enter anything. Add your own rate only if you want a different one from the calculated rate, for example the exact one from the GFŘ notice.
rate.annualOverrideHint: Your rate takes priority over the calculated one for that year and currency.
rate.duplicate: Each year and currency can be listed only once.
rate.hintEur: How an amount in a foreign currency is converted to EUR. The rate is saved with the document when it is issued and does not change after that.

rate.noneHintEcb: The document won't show a conversion to EUR. The ECB rate is still saved for your reports.
rate.nonePayerEcb: A VAT payer must state the VAT in euros on the invoice (§ 74(1)(i) of the Slovak VAT Act), so this option isn't available. Invoices are issued with the ECB rate.

import.title: Switch from another system
import.description: Bring over contacts and issued invoices from your old system. You see a preview first; nothing is saved until you confirm.
import.readOnly: Only the company's owner or an admin can run an import.

step1.title: Export from the old system
step1.hint: A plain CSV file is enough (semicolon, comma or tab separated, UTF-8 or Windows-1250). Column names are recognised automatically: Czech, Slovak and English.

fakturoid.name: Fakturoid
steps: The quickest way is a direct connection: in Fakturoid open your user account settings and copy the Client ID and Client secret from the API v3 section.
Fill them in at step 3 below. We load invoices, proformas, corrections, your whole address book, exchange rates, payments and the original PDFs. You can then skip the contacts step.
Without the connection, export both the invoice list and the contacts to CSV and upload them below, contacts first.

idoklad.name: iDoklad
steps: In the list of issued invoices, select the invoices and export them to Excel or CSV.
If you got an Excel file, save it as CSV (UTF-8).
Export contacts from the address book the same way.

bitfaktura.name: bitfaktura
steps: The quickest way is a direct connection: in BitFaktura open Settings → Account settings → Integration and copy the API authorization code.

Fill in the account name (e.g. company from company.bitfaktura.cz) and the code in step 3 below. We load the invoices and your whole contact list (including contacts you haven't invoiced yet), exchange rates and payment methods. You can then skip the contacts CSV in step 2.
Without the code, you can export the invoices to CSV and upload the file below.

faktorio.name: faktorio
steps: Export your issued invoices and contacts to CSV.
Upload contacts first, then invoices.

invoiceNinja.name: Invoice Ninja
steps: In Settings, open Import | Export and export Invoices and Clients to CSV.
Upload the clients as contacts first, then the invoices.

excel.name: Excel / other
steps: Download the template below, or use your own sheet with invoice number, customer, issue date and amount.
One row = one invoice. Several rows with the same number become one invoice with several items (columns Item, Quantity, Unit price).
Save the sheet as CSV and upload it below.

superfaktura.name: SuperFaktura
steps: In the invoice overview, filter the period you want to move.
Download the list as Excel (.xlsx) or CSV.
Export the client directory the same way and upload it first.

vyfakturuj.name: Vyfakturuj
steps: In the document list, filter issued invoices for the period you want to move.
Download them as CSV or Excel. If the export offers line items, include them and we will bring over every invoice line.
Export contacts separately and upload them first.

kros.name: KROS Fakturácia
steps: In the list of issued invoices, select the documents to move.
Export the list to Excel (.xlsx) or CSV.
Export your customers from the partner list and upload them first.

billdu.name: Billdu
steps: In the Billdu web app, open the invoice list and find the document export.
Choose CSV or Excel and the period you want to move.
Export clients separately and upload them first.

step2.hint: Contacts are matched by company ID (IČO), otherwise by name. Existing contacts are filled in, nothing is deleted. You can skip this step: the invoice import creates missing customers itself.
step2.lead: Optional but recommended: you also bring over contacts you haven't invoiced yet.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: Terms of use of the Billanta invoicing service. The service is for businesses only (B2B). The operator's liability is limited, see section 10.

sections.title: Operator and scope
body: Billanta is operated by {operator} (the "operator").

Billanta is a web application (SaaS) for issuing invoices and related documents, keeping records of customers, payments and expenses, and exporting data. These terms govern the relationship between the operator and anyone who creates an account (the "user").

sections.title: Businesses only (B2B)
body: The service is intended solely for businesses and legal entities using it in the course of their trade or profession (sections 420 et seq. of the Czech Civil Code, Act No. 89/2012 Coll.). It is not intended for consumers.

By creating an account the user declares that they are at least 18 years old and act as a business. The service is not intended for anyone under 18, and the operator does not knowingly collect their personal data, except in the classroom mode for schools under section 17. Consumer protection rules, including the right to withdraw from a distance contract, therefore do not apply. If the operator finds that a user is a consumer, it may close the account.

sections.title: Account and security
body: The user is responsible for the accuracy of their account details and for keeping access secure: passwords, API keys, Telegram or WhatsApp links and bank connection tokens. The user is responsible for anything done through their account or keys.
Suspected misuse of an account must be reported to the operator without delay.

sections.title: Licence and prohibited use
body: For the term of the agreement the operator grants the user a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the service for the user's business. Without the operator's consent the service may not be resold, rented out or made available to anyone outside the user's team, nor copied, decompiled or reverse engineered.

In particular it is prohibited to: issue fictitious, false or fraudulent documents; send unsolicited commercial messages through the service; upload content that infringes third-party rights or the law; circumvent plan limits or technical restrictions; scrape content outside the API; load-test or probe the service for vulnerabilities without the operator's written consent; use the service for money laundering, sanctions evasion or any other unlawful activity.
If this section is breached, the operator may restrict or block e-mail sending, API keys or the whole account without prior notice.

sections.title: Service "as is" and availability
body: The service is provided as is and as available. The operator does not guarantee uninterrupted or error-free availability, agrees no service level (SLA), and does not warrant that the service is fit for any particular purpose of the user.

The service may be interrupted for maintenance, updates, supplier outages (hosting, banks, business registers, AI providers, e-mail) or other reasons. An outage, delay or loss of a feature gives no right to a discount or to damages unless the operator expressly states otherwise.

Unavailability caused by force majeure, internet, power or supplier outages, third-party attacks or planned maintenance is not a breach of the agreement. The operator performs maintenance outside business hours where possible and announces longer planned outages in advance in the app or by e-mail.
This section does not exclude liability that cannot be excluded under section 10.

The user should regularly download or back up their documents (PDF, ISDOC, exports, backups to their own storage). Billanta does not replace the statutory archiving of accounting records, which is the user's obligation.

sections.title: No tax, accounting or legal advice
body: Billanta is a tool for creating documents. Hints, default VAT rates, reverse-charge wording, pre-filled tax forms and any other content in the app are for information only and are not tax, accounting or legal advice.

The same applies to the calculators, guides and tax and insurance estimates on the website and in the app, and to the files they produce. Results are rough estimates with no warranty, do not take every circumstance of the user into account and must be checked before use. To the extent the law allows, the operator is not liable for loss arising from decisions based on them.

sections.title: Responsibility for document content
body: The user alone is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of every document they issue, send or export. This includes amounts, VAT rates and treatment, customer details, issue, supply and due dates, numbering series, and all particulars required by VAT and accounting law.

The same applies to exports for accounting software (ISDOC, UBL, Pohoda, Money S3, CSV), to figures for tax returns and VAT control statements, and to emails and reminders sent from the service. The user must check them before use.

sections.title: AI-generated drafts
body: Invoices created from a voice message, text or a scanned document are always only drafts. AI can be wrong, for example about the amount, the customer or the VAT rate. By clicking "Issue" the user takes full responsibility for the document's content, however the draft was created.

sections.title: Data from registries, banks and other services
body: Company details are loaded from public registries (ARES, RPO, VIES) as they are recorded there. Exchange rates come from the Czech National Bank. Account transactions are fetched from the bank through an interface the user enabled (e.g. the Fio API). The operator does not warrant the accuracy, completeness or availability of these sources, nor that a payment is matched to the right invoice.
Billanta never makes payments from the user's account. Bank connections are read-only.

When the user connects the service to third-party platforms (Telegram, WhatsApp, a bank, Google Drive, a payment gateway, their own webhooks), their terms apply as well. The operator is not liable for changes to, restrictions of or discontinuation of those services, or for a connection stopping to work because of them.

sections.title: Limitation of liability
body: To the extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for indirect or consequential loss. This includes lost profit, loss of data or business, fines, penalties, late-payment interest and additional tax assessments, and loss caused by an outage or unavailability of the service, by suppliers' errors, or by document content under sections 7 to 9.

The operator's total liability for all loss arising in connection with the service is limited to the amount the user actually paid the operator for the service in the 3 months before the event that caused the loss. For free use it is limited to CZK 500.
The limitation does not apply to damage caused intentionally or by gross negligence, nor to harm to a person's natural rights (Section 2898 of the Czech Civil Code).

The user shall compensate the operator for damage and reasonable costs (including legal fees) arising from third-party claims relating to documents, messages or data the user uploaded to or sent from the service, or to a breach of section 4, except where the damage was caused by the operator.
Claims for damages against the operator are subject to a one-year limitation period (Section 630 of the Czech Civil Code).
The user declares that they have read and understood this section and expressly accept it. They consider the amount of the cap reasonable given the price of the service.

sections.title: API, webhooks and integrations
body: The API is meant for connecting the user's own systems. The operator may set request limits per plan and temporarily restrict or revoke an API key whose use endangers the stability of the service or breaches these terms.
The operator may extend and change the API. Retiring an API version or making a backwards-incompatible change will be announced at least 30 days in advance, except for changes required for security.
The user is responsible for securing API keys, for webhook target addresses and for the processing of data that leaves the service through the API or webhooks.

sections.title: Subscription and payments
body: Paid plans are paid in advance for the chosen period through a payment gateway (Stripe or GoPay). Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled. The user can cancel at any time in settings, effective at the end of the paid period. Unused parts of a period are not refunded.

The operator may change the price, in particular due to inflation or changes in costs or in the scope of the service. A change is announced at least 30 days in advance and applies from the next billing period; the price of a period already paid does not change. A user who disagrees may cancel the subscription at the end of the current period.

If a payment is more than 7 days overdue, the operator may switch the account to read-only and export mode. If it is more than 60 days overdue, the operator may terminate the agreement. Data remain available for export under section 13.
The operator may change the scope and limits of the free plan. Free use gives no right to keep any particular feature.

sections.title: User data and termination
body: Data the user puts into the service belongs to the user, who can export it at any time. The operator processes the personal data of the user's customers as a processor under the Data Processing Agreement (DPA), which forms part of these terms.

The user may close the account at any time. The operator may suspend or close an account for breach of these terms, abuse of the service or overdue payment under section 12, and will give notice by e-mail in advance except in urgent cases. After closure the data remain available for export for 30 days, then they are deleted (from backups within 90 days at the latest) unless the law requires otherwise.

Before closing the account the user must export the documents they are required to archive (tax documents usually for 10 years). Once the export period has passed, the operator cannot restore them. Restoring data the user deleted themselves is not guaranteed.
The operator may close a free account nobody has signed in to for more than 12 months, after an e-mail warning at least 30 days in advance.

sections.title: User content and reporting illegal content
body: The single point of contact for users and for EU Member State authorities and the European Commission under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act, DSA) is the operator's e-mail given in section 1. You can write in Czech, Slovak or English.

Users are responsible for the content they publish through the service (public company profile, client portal with invoices, attachments, logo). Anyone can report content they consider illegal by e-mail or, for a public invoice, with the “Report a suspicious document” link. A report should state the reason, the exact address (URL) of the content, the reporter's name and e-mail, and a statement that it is made in good faith.

We review reports without undue delay, confirm receipt to the reporter and tell them the outcome. If we remove or disable content, we tell the user why and how to contest the decision (by replying to our e-mail). Repeated or manifestly illegal content may lead to suspension of the account under section 4.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
body: The operator may change these terms. It will announce any material change by email at least 30 days in advance. The user may terminate the contract before the change takes effect. Continued use after that date means the user accepts the change.
Notices under these terms are delivered to the account e-mail and are deemed delivered on the day they are sent. The user is responsible for keeping the account e-mail up to date.

sections.title: Governing law and disputes
body: The contract is governed by the law of the Czech Republic, excluding conflict-of-law rules and the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Disputes are decided by the Czech courts with jurisdiction over the operator's registered office.
The operator may assign the agreement to a successor taking over the operation of the service; the user consents to this in advance and will be notified.
These terms are issued in Czech, Slovak and English. In case of conflict the Czech version prevails.
If any provision is invalid, the rest remain in force.

sections.title: Classroom mode (schools)
body: As an exception to section 2, the operator offers schools a separate educational classroom mode. A class is set up by a teacher whom the operator has verified, and pupils under 18 may join it. Pupils are not users under these terms and do not create their own account with an email and password.

Pupils join a class with only the class code and a nickname, without an email. They work in practice companies with made-up data, AI features are off in classes, and documents carry a practice-document watermark. They are not tax documents, and the classroom mode must not be used for real business.

For pupils’ personal data the school, acting through the teacher, is the controller and the operator is only a processor under a separate school data processing contract. The teacher confirms that they may act for the school and tells pupils not to enter real personal data.
A class’s practice companies are read-only for 30 days after the class ends and are then deleted. A pupil whom the teacher removes from the class is deleted at once. The classroom mode is free.

sections.title: The “Made with Billanta” line
body: Documents issued in the service carry a short line in the footer, “Made with Billanta” (“Vystaveno v aplikaci Billanta” in Czech, “Vystavené v aplikácii Billanta” in Slovak), linking to the Billanta website. It appears in the PDF, in emails with documents and reminders, and on the online document page.
The link carries the issuer’s referral code, so a business that signs up through it counts towards the referral programme under section 19. It contains no data about the customer or the document.

On the free plan the line is always shown. On a paid plan and during a trial the user can turn it off in Settings under invoices. When the paid plan ends, the line is shown again. Documents made with public tools without an account (such as the reminder generator) always carry it.

sections.title: Referral and partner programme
body: Users can invite other businesses with their invite link. A new business that signs up through it gets welcome credits. The inviter gets as many credits as the new business pays, excluding VAT, for its first plan payment, up to the amount shown in the app. The current rewards are always shown on the referral page in the app. 1 credit equals CZK 1.

The reward is credited after the new business’s second monthly payment, or 30 days after the first payment for a yearly or prepaid plan. If the new business refunds or cancels the payment before then, no reward arises.
The partner programme for accountants and accounting firms works the same way. It is only for accountants whose listing in the accountant directory the operator has approved.

Self-referral is not allowed. No reward arises for a business the inviter owns, or for a business that shares a user with the inviter. Each business counts at most once. If the programme is abused, the operator may withdraw the reward and end the user’s participation.

Credits can only be used to pay for Billanta plans. They have no cash value and cannot be paid out or transferred to another business. Credits do not expire while the business’s account exists and lapse when the account is closed.
The operator may change or end the programme. It will announce the change at least 30 days in advance in the app or by email. Credits granted until then can still be used under this section.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: How Billanta processes the personal data of account users, website visitors and the customers named on invoices (GDPR).

sections.title: Controller and processor
body: The controller of personal data of account users and website visitors is {operator}.
For customer data that users put into the service (contacts, invoices), the user is the controller and Billanta is only a processor under the Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
For pupils in the classroom mode the school is the controller, see section 15.

sections.title: What we process
body: Account data: name, email, password hash or Google sign-in identity, team role, settings.
Company and billing data: business name, company ID, VAT number, address, bank account, logo, issued documents, payments, expenses.
Customer data in documents: names, company IDs, VAT numbers, addresses, contact persons' emails and phone numbers.
Technical data: IP address, browser type, sign-in records and security logs. Analytics only with consent; see section 7.
When AI features are used: the voice messages, texts and document photos the user sends for processing.

sections.title: Purposes and legal bases
body: Providing the service under the contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
Legal obligations, especially accounting and tax. Subscription payment records are kept for 10 years (Art. 6(1)(c)).
Legitimate interest: service security, abuse prevention and enforcing claims (Art. 6(1)(f)).

Consent: analytics cookies in the regions where it is required (Art. 6(1)(a)); consent can be withdrawn at any time. Elsewhere, our legitimate interest in improving the site (Art. 6(1)(f)), which you can object to at any time by turning analytics off in Cookie settings.

sections.title: Processors and recipients
body: Hosting and database: OVHcloud (OVH Hosting Inc.), a virtual server in a data centre in Canada. Canada is covered by a European Commission adequacy decision, see section 5.
Resend: sending email (invoices, reminders, account verification).
Stripe and GoPay: subscription payments. Card details are processed only by these gateways; Billanta never sees them.
Anthropic: AI invoice drafts from text and images. OpenAI: transcribing voice messages to text. Both only when the user uses an AI feature.

Google: Google sign-in and backups to the user’s own Google Drive, only if the user enables them. We also keep encrypted nightly backups of the whole database on the operator’s Google Drive, see section 10.
Telegram and Meta (WhatsApp): only if the user links their account to a chat app.
Microsoft (Clarity): analytics on public pages (only with consent where it is required).

Beyond that, data goes only where the user sends it: their bank or PayPal through a connection they enabled (Fio, PSD2 via Enable Banking, PayPal), their own webhooks and backup storage, and emails to their customers. Lookups in public registries (ARES, RPO, VIES) contain only a company ID or VAT number.
The current list of processors, with the date of its last change, is always kept in this section.

sections.title: Transfers outside the EU
body: The server running the app and the database is in Canada. That transfer relies on the European Commission's adequacy decision for Canada (2002/2/EC, Art. 45 GDPR).

Some processors (Anthropic, OpenAI, Stripe, Microsoft, Google, Resend) may process data in the USA. Transfers rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework where the recipient is certified, and otherwise on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses (Art. 46 GDPR).

sections.title: Retention
body: Account data is kept while the account exists and for 30 days after it is closed. It is then deleted, except data we must keep by law (e.g. subscription payment records for 10 years). It is removed from backups within 90 days at the latest. A free account nobody has signed in to for more than 12 months may be closed after prior notice.
The user's documents stay in the account until the user deletes them or closes the account. The user is responsible for archiving them for the statutory period.

The operator does not archive voice messages and images sent to the AI service after processing; only the resulting invoice draft is stored. AI providers may retain them briefly under their own terms (e.g. for abuse monitoring) and do not use them to train models.
Security logs are kept for at most 12 months.

sections.title: Cookies and analytics
body: Necessary cookies (sign-in, language, cookie choice) are always used. Analytics cookies (Microsoft Clarity) are used only on public pages, never inside the invoicing app, and only with consent in the EU/EEA and other regions where the law requires it. If the browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as declining analytics. See the Cookie Policy for details.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and data portability, and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interest. You can withdraw consent at any time.

Send requests to [contact@billanta.cz]. We will respond within one month. You can lodge a complaint with the Czech Office for Personal Data Protection (www.uoou.cz) or the supervisory authority in your country.

sections.title: Security
body: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS). Each company's data is isolated in the database (row-level security). Sensitive keys (bank tokens, AI keys, backup configurations) are stored encrypted. Access to production data is limited to the people who need it.

sections.title: Backups
body: We back up the whole database of the service every night. The backup is encrypted on the server with age, using a public key. The private key that opens a backup is not on the server; the operator keeps it offline. The encrypted backups are kept on the server, with a copy on the operator’s Google Drive. Without the private key nobody can read them, not even someone with access to the server or the Google account. Backups are deleted after 90 days at the latest (section 6).

Separately, a business can turn on backups of its own data: to its own Google Drive, to its own SFTP server, through a webhook, or as a download. These backups go only where the user sets them to, and the user can encrypt them with their own age key or a passphrase. On Google Drive, Billanta can only access the files it created. The user is responsible for the storage they choose.

sections.title: Newsletter
body: We send the newsletter only to people who sign up and confirm through a link in an email (double opt-in). Unconfirmed sign-ups are deleted within 30 days.
We store the email address, language, country, chosen topics, where you signed up, the consent wording and the times of sign-up and confirmation. The legal basis is consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

You can unsubscribe at any time with one click in the footer of every issue. After that we send nothing more and keep only a record of the consent and the unsubscribe, so we can show we wrote to you lawfully.

sections.title: Where new users come from
body: When you reach the website from a link with campaign parameters (utm) or from another website, we remember the source of the visit in the billanta_src cookie for 90 days: the utm parameters, only the domain of the referring site (no path or query), the first page you visited and the time. If you then create an account, we store this with it so we know which channels bring us users.
We set this cookie only if you have allowed analytics cookies. The legal basis is consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

sections.title: Referral programme
body: When you arrive through an invite link, we keep the inviter’s code in the billanta_ref cookie for 30 days so the invite counts when you sign up.

For the business we then record who invited it, when it signed up, when and how much it paid for a plan, the reward status and credit movements. The purpose is to grant rewards and prevent abuse of the programme (contract and legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR).
The inviter does not see the name or details of the invited business, only a sequence number, whether it pays and how many credits they got for it.

sections.title: Public directories
body: Business directory: a business appears in it only if it turns on its public profile and, in it, the directory listing (off by default). The listing shows the business name, a short description, trade, town, country, logo, and the city only if the business shows its address on the profile. The directory never shows the company ID, email or phone.

Accountant directory: the accountant or accounting firm submits the listing itself, and it is published only after the operator approves it. It shows the name, description, regions, whether they work remotely, services, languages, an indicative price, a contact email or website, and a link to the public profile if that is on.
We publish both listings at the business’s request, and the business can edit, turn off or withdraw them at any time.

sections.title: Classroom mode
body: In the classroom mode the controller of pupils’ personal data is the school, acting through the teacher who sets up the class. The operator is only a processor under the school data processing contract, which we will publish on the School contract page.

Pupils join a class with only the class code and a nickname, without an email or password. We store the nickname, the content of the practice company with made-up data, the personal code for coming back (encrypted and as a hash) and technical data needed to run the service and prevent abuse. AI features are off and pupils’ pages have no analytics.

A class’s practice companies are deleted 30 days after the class ends, and a pupil removed by the teacher at once. A simplified Classroom privacy notice is meant for pupils and parents. Requests about pupils’ data are handled by the school.
Teachers’ data (name, email, school, subject) is processed by the operator as controller under this policy, to verify teachers and run their accounts.

dpa.title: Data Processing Agreement (DPA)
dpa.intro: Agreement on processing personal data under Art. 28 GDPR between the user (controller) and the operator (processor), part of the Terms of Service.

sections.title: Parties and subject
body: The controller is the user of Billanta. The processor is {operator}.
The processor processes the personal data that the controller puts into the service only as far as needed to provide the service under the Terms of Service, and for as long as they are in force.

sections.title: Nature, purpose and scope
body: Purpose: issuing and sending documents, keeping records of contacts, payments and expenses, exporting and backing up data, and AI document drafts if the controller uses them.
Data subjects: the controller's customers and suppliers and their contact persons, and members of the controller's team.

Categories of data: identification and contact data (name, company, company ID, VAT ID, address, e-mail, phone), payment and invoicing data including bank account numbers and account transactions and, where the controller uses AI features, voice messages, texts and photos of documents. Special categories of data (Art. 9 GDPR) are not processed and the controller should not upload them.

sections.title: Processor obligations
body: Process data only on the controller's documented instructions. The controller's configuration and use of the service count as instructions.
Inform the controller immediately if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other data protection law.
Transfer data to third countries only in line with the controller's instructions and Chapter V GDPR, as described in the Privacy Policy (section 5).
Ensure that everyone with access to the data is bound by confidentiality.
Take appropriate technical and organisational measures under Art. 32 GDPR: encryption in transit, isolation of each controller's data, encrypted key storage, access control and backups.
Help the controller handle data subject requests and meet its obligations under Art. 32–36 GDPR.
Notify the controller of a personal data breach without undue delay, and at the latest within 48 hours of becoming aware of it.

sections.title: Sub-processors
body: The controller gives general authorisation to engage the sub-processors listed in the Privacy Policy (section 4).

The processor will tell the controller of any intended change by email at least 14 days in advance. The controller may object on reasonable grounds or terminate the contract. The processor will impose the same data protection obligations on its sub-processors.

In an urgent change for security or operational reasons the processor may engage a new sub-processor immediately and inform the controller without undue delay. The processor remains fully liable to the controller for the performance of its sub-processors' obligations (Art. 28(4) GDPR).

sections.title: Termination, deletion and audit
body: After the agreement ends, the processor lets the controller export the data for 30 days. Then, at the controller's choice, it deletes them or returns them as an export, unless the law requires them to be kept. Data are removed from backups within 90 days at the latest.

The processor will give the controller the information needed to show compliance with this agreement. An on-site audit is possible by prior arrangement, at the controller's cost and at most once a year.

The limitation of liability in the Terms (section 10) applies to the parties' liability under this agreement. It does not apply to claims of data subjects under Art. 82 GDPR to the extent they cannot be limited by contract.

classroomPrivacy.title: Privacy in class
classroomPrivacy.intro: A short explanation for pupils, students and their parents: what Billanta stores when you join a class, and who can see it.

sections.title: What we store
body: The nickname you choose. Don’t use your full name; a nickname your teacher will recognise is enough.
Your practice company and everything you create in it: invoices, customers, expenses and other records. The data is made up, so don’t enter real details about yourself or anyone else.
Your personal code for getting back to your company. We store it encrypted.
A few technical details the service needs to run and to prevent abuse, such as how many attempts to get in failed.

sections.title: What we don’t store or use
body: We don’t ask for your email, phone number or a password.
There is no artificial intelligence (AI), analytics or advertising in class. We don’t send you anything and don’t use your data for marketing.

sections.title: Who can see your data
body: Your teacher, and any other teachers of the same class, can see your company. They can only look; they don’t change anything in it. Your classmates can’t see your company.
People at Billanta only access the data when it is necessary for support or security.

sections.title: When your data is deleted
body: After the class ends you can still look at your company for 30 days. Then it is deleted, together with your nickname and personal code. It disappears from encrypted backups within 90 days at the latest.
If your teacher removes you from the class, your company is deleted straight away.

sections.title: Who to contact
body: Your school decides about your data in class. Billanta only processes it for the school under a contract with the school. With a question or a request to delete your data, talk to your teacher or the school.
Parents can ask the school for details, or write to the operator of Billanta: {operator}.

about.title: About Billanta
about.lead: Billanta is an invoicing tool built on top of the open standards that already run Czech and Slovak invoicing – not around them.
about.whatBody: Billanta issues invoices in the ISDOC format, pulls counterparty details straight from the ARES business registry, and keeps your numbering sequence and VAT rates consistent, so you're not stuck copying last month's spreadsheet template. You can also send a voice note over Telegram or WhatsApp and Billanta will turn it into a draft invoice ready for a quick check – it's only final once you confirm it yourself.
about.whoBody: We're building this for freelancers and small businesses in Czech Republic and Slovakia – people who invoice themselves between client meetings, not a finance department with its own IT staff.
about.whyBody: Invoicing always took us longer than it should have – looking up a company ID in ARES, tracking the next invoice number by hand, opening a laptop just to bill one line item on the way back from a client. We wanted something that handles that part and leaves us to decide only what actually matters: whether the invoice is right before it goes out.

page.title: Cookie Policy
page.intro: The cookies and similar storage Billanta uses, what each one is for, and how long it lasts.

session.purpose: Keeps you signed in. The demo and pupils joining a class use the same cookie.
session.duration: 30 days; for a demo or class, until it ends

csrf.purpose: Protects the sign-in form against forgery and returns you to the page you came from.

oauth.purpose: Secures signing in with Google or another provider. Only while you sign in.

tenant.purpose: Remembers which company you are working in inside the app.
tenant.duration: 1 year; for a demo or class, until it ends

demoTransfer.purpose: Lets you carry the demo data over into a newly created account.

consent.purpose: Stores your choice in this cookie dialog.

region.purpose: Remembers whether analytics needs consent in your region, so it is not looked up on every visit (in the browser, never sent to the server).

theme.purpose: Remembers light or dark theme (in the browser, never sent to the server).

referral.purpose: The referral code from a link another user invited you with, so their reward is credited when you sign up. Only when you arrive through such a link.

promo.purpose: A promo or event code from a link (?promo= or /join/CODE), so it applies to your new company. Only when you arrive through such a link.

switch.purpose: The app you are moving from (a "Switch from…" link to signup), so the welcome screen offers its import. Only when you sign up through such a link.

invoiceFilters.purpose: Quick filters of the invoice list in the app.

preferences.purpose: Small choices and unfinished input in the app and tools: collapsed sections, chart type, dismissed tips, supplier details in the no-signup invoice form. They stay in the browser and are never sent to the server.
preferences.duration: Until deleted or the tab closes

attribution.purpose: Where you first came from: campaign tags (utm_*), the site that linked here (domain only) and the first page. Saved with your account when you sign up, so we know which channels work. Only with analytics consent.

clarity.purpose: Microsoft Clarity: traffic measurement, heatmaps and session recordings. Only with consent.

page.functionalNote: Functional cookies are created only when you use a link that needs them (an invite, a promo code, moving from another app) or a choice in the app, and serve only what you meant by that link or choice. That is why we do not ask for consent for them. We do not share them with anyone.
page.analyticsNote: Analytics cookies are used only on the public pages (home, pricing, information pages). No analytics ever runs inside the app, where you work with invoices and customer data. In the EU/EEA, the UK, Switzerland, Brazil, Canada and the US states where recording a visit needs every party's consent (e.g. California, Pennsylvania, Florida, Washington), we turn them on only with your consent; if we cannot tell where you are, we ask too. Elsewhere they run by default and you can turn them off at any time. Your location is estimated only from the country and state reported by the network that delivers the site, and is not stored. Clarity is operated by Microsoft; data may be processed outside the EU under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal, we treat it everywhere as "Essential only" and do not show the cookie banner at all.
page.attributionNote: Where you came from (billanta_src) is not stored anywhere before you consent: it is only held in the open page's memory, and the cookie is written once you allow analytics. If you refuse or withdraw consent, we delete it.
page.schoolsNote: On the pages for schools (/for-schools), for joining a class (/join) and in a pupil's class access we run no analytics at all, even with consent: children use them and cannot give valid consent themselves. The cookie banner does not open there by itself.
page.withdraw: You can change or withdraw consent at any time with the button below or the “Cookie settings” link in the site footer.

peppol.intro: You may want to send this as a UBL e-invoice over the Peppol network (in Slovakia, VAT payers must issue them to domestic businesses from 1 January 2027). An access point would reject or flag it because of:

code.vatInvalid: VAT number has an invalid format
code.vatMissing: VAT number is missing, but this VAT treatment needs it
code.endpointMissing: no Peppol electronic address (add a VAT number with an EU country prefix)
code.skDicMissing: the Slovak DIČ (10 digits) is missing; the Peppol address 0245 is built from it
code.precedingMissing: the credit note does not reference the original invoice it corrects

requirements.title: Fill in the mandatory details before issuing
requirements.titleIssued: This document is missing mandatory details

code.addressIncomplete: registered address is missing (street or city)
code.dicMissingReverse: reverse charge needs the customer's VAT number
code.registryMissing: the public-register entry is missing (e.g. trade licence register), add it in Settings › Company

net.toggle: Fees and exchange rate (PayPal, Stripe, Wise…)
net.hint: Optional. From the fees and the amount actually credited we work out the net proceeds and the exchange difference.
net.title: Net proceeds
net.noReceived: Enter the amount credited in {home} to see the exchange difference too.

correction.title: Edited after sending
correction.body: You sent this invoice to the customer on {date} and it has changed since. They have the old version – send them the corrected one. The public link already shows the new one.
correction.sendBody: The customer gets an email titled “Corrected invoice” explaining that it replaces the earlier version. The send is recorded in the change history.
correction.editNote: You already sent this invoice to the customer ({date}). After editing, the detail page will offer to send them the corrected version.

invite.title: Team invitation
invite.heading: Invitation to {company}
invite.accepted: You are now a team member.
invite.alreadyAccepted: This invitation has already been accepted.
invite.expired: This invitation has expired. Ask for a new one.
invite.emailMismatch: This invitation is for {email}. Sign in with that email.
invite.notFoundHint: The link is invalid or the invitation was revoked.

templates.title: Invoice templates
templates.lead: Save recurring invoices as a template and issue them in one click – one at a time or in bulk for several customers. Create a template from any document via “Save as template”, or start from a ready-made starter.
templates.emptyHint: Open any invoice and choose “Save as template” in its menu. Or start from a starter below.
templates.deleteBody: Template “{name}” will be deleted. Documents created from it stay unchanged.
templates.startersHint: A pre-filled form with typical items – just add the customer and prices.
templates.name: Name

hourly.name: Hourly work
hourly.description: Consulting, development or services billed by the hour.

retainer.name: Monthly retainer
retainer.description: A regular monthly service – management, support, maintenance.

advance.name: Project advance
advance.description: A proforma invoice before work starts.

quote.name: Project quote
quote.description: A quote split into project phases.

bulk.title: Bulk invoicing
bulk.lead: Pick a template and customers – each gets their own document with the same items. Great for retainers, memberships or rent.
bulk.noTemplatesHint: Bulk invoicing starts from a saved template. Create one from an existing invoice or from a starter in the gallery.
bulk.issueNowHint: Otherwise drafts are created for you to review before issuing.
bulk.summary: This creates {count, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}} worth {total} excl. VAT in total.
bulk.submitDrafts: Create {count, plural, one {# draft} other {# drafts}}
bulk.submitIssue: Issue {count, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}}
bulk.doneDrafts: Created {count, plural, one {# draft} other {# drafts}}.
bulk.doneIssued: Issued {count, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}}.
