notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty: Nothing new yet. We'll let you know when something happens.

qrScan.title: Scan the invoice QR code
qrScan.hint: Point the camera at the QR payment or QR invoice code on the document. The image is processed on your device only.
qrScan.denied: No camera access. Allow it in your browser, or upload a photo of the document.
qrScan.unsupported: This browser doesn't support the camera. Upload a photo or PDF instead.

dictation.denied: The microphone isn't allowed. Allow it in your browser, or type the text.

netEstimate.label: You keep
netEstimate.hint: Rough Czech sole-trader estimate: the amount without VAT minus income tax (15 %), social and health insurance on this invoice – about {burden}. Uses the chosen flat rate and ignores minimum advances and tax credits. See Exports for the full year.

welcome.title: Welcome to Billanta
welcome.subtitle: Three quick questions and the app shows only what you'll actually use. You can change everything later in Settings.
welcome.companyHint: Type your company name, your own name (sole trader) or IČO and we fill in the invoice details from ARES, the Slovak RPO or foreign registers. You can also skip this.
welcome.businessTitle: How do you run your business?
welcome.businessHint: We'll switch on the modules that fit.
welcome.modulesTitle: What do you want to use?
welcome.modulesHint: Invoicing is always on. Toggle the rest.
welcome.later: Change it anytime in Settings → Modules.
welcome.searchPlaceholder: Company name, your name or IČO
welcome.searchEmpty: Nothing found. Try another name or IČO, or another register.
welcome.importHint: Pick it and once you save, we will walk you through importing contacts, invoices and your number sequence.

featurePages.indexHeading: Everything invoicing needs for freelancers and small businesses
featurePages.indexLead: Each feature has its own page with a description, how it works and answers to common questions. It all comes in one app – no add-ons or extra modules.
featurePages.indexDescription: Invoicing features: QR payments, ISDOC, ARES lookup, reminders, bank payment matching, recurring invoices, Czech VAT returns, Pohoda and Money S3 export.
featurePages.ctaNote: No credit card. Every feature is available right after sign-up.

qr.name: QR payment on invoices
qr.title: QR payment codes on invoices (SPAYD)
qr.description: Every invoice gets a QR payment code following the Czech SPAYD standard. Your customer scans it in their banking app and pays.
qr.lead: Your customer doesn’t retype the account number, amount or variable symbol. They scan the QR code in their bank’s app and the payment is ready.
points: QR code in the SPAYD standard supported by every Czech bank
Account, amount, currency, variable symbol and due date come straight from the invoice
The code is on the PDF and on the online invoice link you send
For a partly paid invoice, the code asks only for the remaining amount
steps: Add your bank account (account number or IBAN) in settings.
Issue an invoice – the QR code is generated automatically.
Your customer scans and pays, and you match the payment to the invoice.

faq.q: Does the QR payment work with every bank?
faq.a: The SPAYD (QR Platba) standard is supported by the mobile apps of all major Czech banks and most Slovak ones.

faq.q: Do I have to turn it on?
faq.a: No. Once your bank account is filled in, invoices show the code automatically.

isdoc.name: ISDOC export
isdoc.title: Invoices in the ISDOC format
isdoc.description: Export invoices as ISDOC, the Czech e-invoicing standard that most accounting software can import.
isdoc.lead: ISDOC is the Czech electronic invoice format. Your accountant imports it without retyping anything.
points: One-click ISDOC export of any invoice
Includes supplier, customer, line items, VAT rates and payment details
Useful for accountants, large customers and public bodies
PDF and CSV downloads are available too
UBL 2.1 e-invoice file (Peppol BIS 3.0) for Slovak customers; sending over Peppol for the 2027 SK mandate is in the works
steps: Issue an invoice as usual.
Choose ISDOC export in the invoice detail.
Send the file to your accountant or customer to import.

faq.q: Who needs ISDOC?
faq.a: Mostly accountants and companies that import invoices automatically. Some public bodies and large firms require e-invoices.

faq.q: Does ISDOC replace the PDF?
faq.a: No, it complements it. Your customer still gets a readable PDF; ISDOC is for machines.

registry.name: Company lookup in ARES and registers
registry.title: Fill in customers from ARES by company ID or name
registry.description: Type a company ID or name and the customer’s details come from ARES. We also search the Slovak RPO, EU VIES and foreign registers.
registry.lead: Type a few letters of the name or the company ID. The address, VAT ID and legal name come from the official register, so no typos on the invoice.
points: Czech companies from ARES by ID or name
Slovak companies from RPO, any EU company by VAT ID via VIES
Foreign registers: France, Norway, Finland, Denmark, Switzerland, Poland, the UK and the worldwide LEI index
Your saved contacts appear instantly, register results stream in
steps: Type the company ID or name into the customer field.
Pick the company – the details fill in.
The customer is saved to your contacts for next time.

faq.q: Is the lookup free?
faq.a: Yes. The registers are public and the lookup is part of the app.

faq.q: Can I find a sole trader by name?
faq.a: Yes. Type the first and last name – ARES matches whole words, so finish at least one word.

reminders.name: Automatic reminders
reminders.title: Automatic payment reminders for overdue invoices
reminders.description: After the due date we email your customer a polite reminder. You choose the interval and the maximum number of reminders.
reminders.lead: Stop tracking who hasn’t paid. Reminders go out automatically once an invoice is overdue.
points: Overdue reminders are emailed automatically
Configurable gap between reminders and a maximum count
Each reminder links to the invoice with its QR payment
Reminders stop as soon as the invoice is paid
steps: Turn on reminders in invoice settings and pick an interval.
An invoice past its due date is marked overdue.
Your customer gets reminders until they pay or the limit is reached.

faq.q: How often are reminders sent?
faq.a: The default gap is 7 days; you can change it and the maximum count in settings.

faq.q: Can I send a reminder manually?
faq.a: Yes, you can send a reminder for an overdue invoice at any time.

bankMatching.name: Bank payment matching
bankMatching.title: Automatic matching of payments to invoices
bankMatching.description: Incoming payments are matched to invoices by variable symbol and amount. Fio, other banks over PSD2 and PayPal sync by themselves; for any other bank, upload a CSV statement.
bankMatching.lead: Instead of ticking off paid invoices by hand, the app assigns payments itself and marks the invoice paid.
points: Fio banka: incoming payments downloaded every hour via the official API
Other banks: statement import in a simple CSV format
Matching by variable symbol, amount and currency
Partial payments are recorded on the invoice as part-payments
Unmatched payments stay for manual assignment
steps: In Bank, connect an account (Fio with a read-only token, other banks over PSD2, or PayPal), or upload a CSV statement from your bank.
The app downloads the payments and matches them to invoices.
Review the remaining unmatched payments and assign them by hand.

faq.q: Which banks are supported?
faq.a: Fio directly over its free API, other Czech, Slovak and EEA banks (Revolut and Wise included) over PSD2 (licensed provider Enable Banking). Any bank also via a CSV statement: we recognise the usual Czech and Slovak bank exports, and date, amount and currency are enough.

faq.q: Can Billanta make payments from my account?
faq.a: No. The Fio token is created with the “view account only” permission, which cannot send anything. We store it encrypted.

faq.q: What if the customer forgets the variable symbol?
faq.a: The payment stays unmatched and you assign it to the invoice manually.

recurring.name: Recurring invoices
recurring.title: Recurring invoices
recurring.description: Set up a recurring invoice for regular services. It is issued automatically every week, month, quarter or year.
recurring.lead: Rent, retainers, website care – invoices you issue the same way every month can issue themselves.
points: Weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly schedules
A template with customer, line items and payment terms
Each new invoice gets the next number in your series
Pause or end the schedule at any time
steps: Create an invoice template and choose a frequency.
On the scheduled day the app issues a new invoice.
Review it or send it straight to your customer.

faq.q: Can I change the amount of a recurring invoice?
faq.a: Yes, edit the template at any time; the change applies to future invoices.

faq.q: Does every invoice get a new number?
faq.a: Yes, each issued invoice takes the next number in your series.

voice.name: Invoice by voice
voice.title: Create invoices by voice via Telegram
voice.description: Dictate an invoice into your phone. AI turns the voice message into a draft invoice that you just review.
voice.lead: On the road and need to bill someone? Send a voice message and the draft will be waiting in the app.
points: Voice messages through a linked Telegram account
AI picks out the customer, items, quantities and prices
It creates a draft – nothing is sent without your review
Works in Czech and Slovak
steps: Link your Telegram in settings.
Say who you are billing and for what.
Review the draft in the app and issue it.

faq.q: Will an invoice go out without my review?
faq.a: No. A voice message only ever creates a draft that you confirm.

faq.q: Do I need to speak formally?
faq.a: No, everyday speech is fine.

expenses.name: Expense tracking
expenses.title: Expense and cost tracking
expenses.description: Record received invoices and expenses in one place and see your income, costs and estimated net profit.
expenses.lead: Expenses belong next to invoices. Track them in the same app and see the real result of your business.
points: Received invoices and expenses including VAT
Categories and search
CSV export for your accountant
Income vs. expenses on the dashboard
steps: Add an expense with supplier, amount and date.
It counts towards your overviews and tax estimate.
Export everything for your accountant at period end.

faq.q: Do expenses go into the VAT return?
faq.a: Yes, expenses with VAT feed the Czech VAT return and control statement exports.

faq.q: Can I export expenses?
faq.a: Yes, as CSV.

vat.name: Czech VAT returns for EPO
vat.title: Czech VAT return, control statement and EC sales list as XML for EPO
vat.description: From your invoices and expenses we prepare the XML files of the Czech VAT return, control statement and EC sales list, ready to upload to the EPO tax portal.
vat.lead: Czech VAT payers don’t retype numbers into forms. Download the XML and upload it to the tax portal.
points: VAT return (DPHDP3) as XML
Control statement (DPHKH1) with every document
EC sales list (DPHSHV) for EU supplies
Files are accepted by the EPO portal and the data box
steps: Issue invoices and record expenses during the period.
Pick the period in Exports and download the XML.
Upload it to EPO, check it and submit.

faq.q: Will the app file the return for me?
faq.a: No. We prepare the file; you upload and submit it yourself and remain responsible for the filing.

faq.q: Is this for non-VAT payers too?
faq.a: Non-payers don’t need these files; they can use the annual income and expense summary.

accounting.name: Exports for your accountant
accounting.title: Export invoices to Pohoda, Money S3 and CSV for your accountant
accounting.description: Export invoices as Pohoda or Money S3 XML, CSV for Excel and an annual income and expense summary.
accounting.lead: Your accountant doesn’t retype anything. Send a file their software can import.
points: Invoice XML export for Pohoda and Money S3
Invoice and expense CSV for Excel or other tools
Annual summary with foreign currencies converted at ČNB rates
Data backups and a download of all documents at once
steps: Open Exports and choose a period.
Pick a format – Pohoda XML, Money S3 XML, CSV or annual summary.
Send the file to your accountant.

faq.q: Do you support accounting software other than Pohoda?
faq.a: Most programs import CSV or ISDOC. For Pohoda and Money S3 we export their own XML formats.

faq.q: How are foreign currencies converted?
faq.a: The annual summary converts foreign-currency invoices at the Czech National Bank rate.

partialPayments.name: Partial payments
partialPayments.title: Partial payments and instalments
partialPayments.description: Record part payments against an invoice and always see how much has been paid and how much is left.
partialPayments.lead: Not every invoice is paid in one go. Track instalments and keep an eye on the balance.
points: Multiple payments per invoice with date and amount
Remaining balance on the invoice, in lists and on the online link
The QR payment asks only for the balance
The invoice is marked paid once the full amount is in
steps: Add a received payment to the invoice.
The app recalculates the balance.
Once fully paid, the invoice is marked paid.

faq.q: Are partial payments matched from statements too?
faq.a: Yes, a statement payment lower than the invoice total is recorded as a partial payment.

faq.q: Do reminders continue after a partial payment?
faq.a: Yes, the invoice stays unpaid until the full amount is in.

integrations.name: API, webhooks and calendar
integrations.title: API, Discord and Slack webhooks, RSS and iCal
integrations.description: Connect invoicing to your other tools: a REST API with keys, webhooks for Discord, Slack and your own systems, an invoice RSS feed and due dates in your calendar.
integrations.lead: Send alerts to your team chat and due dates to your calendar.
points: REST API with your own API keys and documentation
Webhooks when an invoice is paid, viewed or overdue – Discord, Slack or signed JSON
iCal due-date calendar for Google, Apple and Outlook
RSS feed of issued invoices
steps: Webhooks, RSS and the calendar are under Settings → Integrations.
Create an API key under Settings → API keys.
For a webhook, pick the events you want to hear about.

faq.q: How do I verify a webhook came from you?
faq.a: JSON webhooks carry an HMAC X-Billanta-Signature header signed with the secret shown in settings.

faq.q: Is the calendar public?
faq.a: The link contains a secret token known only to whoever you share it with, and you can rotate it at any time.

migration.name: Switch from another system
migration.title: Switch from BitFaktura, Fakturoid, iDoklad or Excel
migration.description: Bring over contacts and your whole invoice history from another invoicing system or from Excel. Preview before saving, no emails sent, numbering continues.
migration.lead: Starting over doesn't mean losing your history. A CSV export from the old system is all you need.
points: Import contacts and issued invoices from CSV
From BitFaktura and Fakturoid straight over the API: invoices, address book and original PDFs
Columns from Fakturoid, iDoklad, faktorio, Invoice Ninja or your own sheet are recognised automatically
Preview with invoice count, period and totals before saving
Multi-item invoices, proformas and credit notes
Nothing is sent and imported invoices get no reminders
Numbering continues after the last imported number
steps: Export contacts and invoices from the old system to CSV.
Upload the files under Settings → Switch from another system.
Check the preview and confirm the import.

faq.q: What if I run the import twice?
faq.a: Invoices whose number you already have are skipped, so you can safely repeat the import, for example with an updated file.

faq.q: Will my clients notice the import?
faq.a: No. Imported invoices are saved as already issued; no emails or reminders are sent.

faq.q: Do I have to upload contacts first?
faq.a: No. The invoice import creates customers you don't have yet. A separate contacts import is useful for clients you haven't invoiced yet.

quotes.name: Quotes and proformas
quotes.title: Quotes and proforma invoices
quotes.description: Send a quote, let the client accept it online and turn it into a proforma or a final invoice in one click. Separate number series for each document type.
quotes.lead: From quote to deposit to final invoice, without retyping anything.
points: Quotes, proforma invoices, invoices and credit notes
The client accepts or rejects a quote online, with a note
Turn a quote into a proforma or invoice in one click
The invoice after a paid proforma is issued as settled by the deposit
Separate number series: ZF for proformas, OD for credit notes, NA for quotes
steps: Create a quote and send the client a link.
The client accepts it and you get notified.
Issue a proforma or invoice from the quote in one click.

faq.q: Is a proforma a tax document?
faq.a: No. The tax document is the invoice issued after the deposit is paid, which the app prepares from the paid proforma.

faq.q: Does the client need an account to accept a quote?
faq.a: No. The link you email them is enough.

currencies.name: Foreign-currency invoices
currencies.title: Invoices in euros and other currencies with ČNB rates
currencies.description: Invoice in EUR, USD and other currencies. The Czech National Bank rate for the taxable supply date is filled in automatically and converted to CZK for VAT.
currencies.lead: Foreign clients pay in their currency, your VAT stays right in crowns.
points: Invoices in euros, dollars and other currencies
ČNB rate for the taxable supply date filled in at issue
The rate can be adjusted by hand
Conversion to CZK for VAT returns and control statements
The invoice shows the bank account in the invoice's currency
Reverse charge for foreign VAT payers
steps: Pick the currency on the invoice.
The ČNB rate is filled in when you issue it.
VAT exports convert the amounts to CZK.

faq.q: Which rate is used?
faq.a: The ČNB rate for the taxable supply date. If it can't be loaded at that moment, it is filled in during the VAT export.

faq.q: Can I have a euro account?
faq.a: Yes. Add several bank accounts in the company settings; the account in the invoice's currency is picked automatically.

team.name: Team and roles
team.title: Invoicing for teams and accountants
team.description: Invite colleagues and your accountant. Owner, admin, accountant and viewer roles, per-area permissions and several companies under one login.
team.lead: Everyone sees and changes only what they should.
points: Email invitations for colleagues and external accountants
Owner, admin, accountant and viewer roles
Separate permissions for invoices, contacts, expenses, bank and reports
Several companies under one login
Company settings and API keys for owners and admins only
steps: Send an invitation under Settings → Team.
Your colleague accepts it and signs in.
Adjust their permissions if needed.

faq.q: Can the accountant only read?
faq.a: Yes. Give them the viewer role, or set individual areas to read-only for the accountant role.

faq.q: Do I pay per user?
faq.a: See the pricing page. Inviting colleagues is part of the app.

bankSync.name: Bank and PayPal sync
bankSync.title: Automatic payment download from your bank and PayPal
bankSync.description: Connect Fio, another bank over PSD2 or PayPal, and incoming payments download and match to invoices by themselves. No statement exports or uploads.
bankSync.lead: Fio offers its clients a free API. Create a read-only token and paste it into Billanta.
points: Incoming payments downloaded every hour, or right away with Sync now
View-only token, stored encrypted and never shown again
Matched invoices are marked paid and you get a notification
Each payment is downloaded only once, even when periods overlap
Pause or disconnect the account any time
Other banks (ČSOB, KB, Česká spořitelna, Tatra banka, Revolut, Wise and other EEA banks) over PSD2, with consent given at the bank itself
PayPal over the Transaction Search API, including the fee it kept, booked on the invoice
steps: In Fio internet banking open Settings → API and add a “view account only” token.
In Billanta go to Bank, click Connect a bank, choose Fio banka and paste the token.
From then on payments download and match on their own.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: Fio's API is free for its clients and the connection is part of Billanta.

faq.q: How far back are payments downloaded?
faq.a: The last 30 days on the first download, then always from the previous download.

faq.q: What about other banks?
faq.a: Over PSD2: in Bank click Connect a bank, choose Bank over PSD2, pick your bank and grant read-only access in its online banking. The connection runs through the licensed provider Enable Banking; consent lasts 90 to 180 days depending on the bank and we remind you before it runs out. Because of PSD2 limits these accounts sync about every 6 hours.

faq.q: And PayPal payments?
faq.a: In Bank click Connect a bank, choose PayPal and paste the Client ID and Secret of your REST app with Transaction search enabled. Received payments are matched by invoice number or variable symbol and amount, and the PayPal fee is booked on the invoice. PayPal publishes transactions with a delay of up to 3 hours.

paymentMethods.name: Custom payment methods
paymentMethods.title: Custom payment methods on invoices
paymentMethods.description: Besides bank transfer, cash, card and cash on delivery, add your own payment methods, such as PayPal or a payment gateway, with instructions on how to pay.
paymentMethods.lead: The customer sees exactly how to pay, and you don't retype the instructions every time.
points: Transfer, cash, card, cash on delivery and “other” are always available
A custom method has a name, a behaviour (like transfer, cash…) and instructions
Instructions are printed on the document below the items
Variables work in instructions, e.g. {amount} or {number}
Ready-made presets to pick from
steps: In Settings → Payment methods add your own method or pick a preset.
Choose it as the payment method in the invoice form.
The instructions are printed on the invoice, and you can still edit them there.

faq.q: Can Billanta accept card payments?
faq.a: Yes. Once you connect your own Stripe account, every invoice gets a Pay by card button and a paid invoice is marked by itself, fee included. PayPal payments are matched once you connect PayPal in Bank. Every invoice also carries a QR payment.

faq.q: Who can change payment methods?
faq.a: The company owner or an admin.

publicProfile.name: Public company profile
publicProfile.title: Public company profile at your own address
publicProfile.description: A simple public page for your business: what you do, what it costs and how to reach you. Put the link in your email signature, on invoices or on social media.
publicProfile.lead: A business card on the web without building a website. Turn it on, fill it in, share the link.
points: Your own profile address, including a subdomain
Description, services with prices and contacts
Live check that the address is free
A disabled profile is hidden and its settings stay saved
steps: In Settings → Public profile choose an address.
Fill in the description, services and contacts.
Publish the profile and copy the link.

faq.q: What happens to the old address after a change?
faq.a: It stops working. Share the new address again.

faq.q: Are my invoices visible on the profile?
faq.a: No. The profile shows only what you write into it.

backups.name: Data backups
backups.title: Automatic backups to your own storage
backups.description: Your company data is regularly exported to your own server over SFTP, to Google Drive or to a webhook – optionally encrypted with your key. You can also download the whole database any time.
backups.lead: You always keep a copy of your invoices and expenses, independent of us.
points: Your own server, NAS or hosting over SFTP with an SSH key
Backups encrypted with age using your key or passphrase
Google Drive: the app sees only the files it creates
Webhook: we send the backup to your server, signed
Manual download of the whole database as an SQLite file
A separate schedule for each destination
steps: In Settings → Data backups add a destination.
Choose how often the backup runs.
Backups are stored automatically and you see their status in the overview.

faq.q: Are backups free?
faq.a: Manual download and saving to your own storage are available on the free plan too.

faq.q: Why back up?
faq.a: A copy on your side is insurance against an outage or the service ending. We recommend keeping it on.

faq.q: Can my data stay only with me?
faq.a: Send backups to your own SFTP server and encrypt them with a key only you hold – nobody else can read the file. Open it with the standard age tool and the SQLite database with any viewer.

templates.name: Templates and bulk invoicing
templates.title: Invoice templates and bulk invoicing
templates.description: Save a recurring invoice as a template and issue it in one click, one at a time or in bulk for many customers.
templates.lead: Bill retainers, membership fees or rent to everyone at once. Each customer gets their own document.
points: A template from any document via “Save as template”
A gallery of ready presets, e.g. advance invoice or rent
Bulk issuing of the same template for selected customers
Each document gets its own number from the number series
steps: Open an invoice and choose Save as template, or pick a preset.
In Bulk invoicing choose the template and customers.
The documents are issued and ready to send.

faq.q: How is this different from recurring invoices?
faq.a: A recurring invoice issues itself on a schedule. A template is used whenever you want, for many customers at once.

aiPrefill.name: AI invoice prefill
aiPrefill.title: An invoice from one sentence with AI
aiPrefill.description: Write “invoice for 27604977, 3 hours of consulting at 1500 CZK” and AI fills in the customer from the registry, the items and prices. You just review and issue.
aiPrefill.lead: AI prepares a draft and never issues anything by itself. Use Billanta's AI, your own key, or turn it off completely.
points: Invoice prefill from text or a voice message
Extraction of receipts and received invoices from a photo or PDF
Billanta's AI with a daily limit, or your own Anthropic key with no limit
Your own key is stored encrypted
Off = no data is sent to AI
The same prefill in the public API
steps: In Settings → AI choose the AI source.
In the invoice form write what you want to bill.
Review the draft and issue it.

faq.q: Can AI make mistakes?
faq.a: Yes, which is why the result is always a draft. Check the details before issuing.

faq.q: Where is the data sent?
faq.a: The text goes to Anthropic's Claude model for processing. With AI turned off nothing is sent.

bilingual.name: Bilingual invoices
bilingual.title: Bilingual invoices for foreign customers
bilingual.description: Labels on the PDF invoice can be in two languages, e.g. “Datum vystavení / Issue date”. Czech, Slovak and English.
bilingual.lead: Your foreign customer understands the invoice, and so does your local accountant.
points: Second label language: Czech, Slovak or English
The whole app and emails in three languages
Invoices in foreign currency with exchange-rate conversion
If the invoice is already in that language, it stays single-language
steps: In Settings → Invoices choose the second PDF language.
Issue the invoice as usual.
The PDF has labels in both languages.

faq.q: Are item texts translated too?
faq.a: No. The document labels are bilingual; you write the items as you need.

emails.name: Emails and variables
emails.title: Custom email texts and variables on documents
emails.description: Edit the invoice and reminder emails and insert variables like '{number}', '{due_date}' or your own text into them and into document notes.
emails.lead: Write the text once; the real details are filled in when it is sent.
points: Custom text for the invoice and reminder emails
An empty field uses the default text
Variables like {number}, {due_date}, {vs} or {customer}
Your own variables usable in emails and notes
Numeric variables in formulas of custom invoice fields
steps: In Settings → Customer emails edit the texts.
Click a variable to insert it at the cursor.
On sending, variables are replaced with the document's details.

faq.q: Where is the list of variables?
faq.a: In Settings → Variables, where you can also add your own.

requirements.name: Mandatory details check
requirements.title: Mandatory invoice details check
requirements.description: Billanta warns you before issuing when an invoice is missing a detail required by Czech or Slovak VAT or commercial law – company ID, VAT number, address.
requirements.lead: An invoice missing a mandatory detail may be unusable for your customer. Billanta checks it before you send it and tells you exactly what to add.
points: Checks tax document requirements under § 29 of the Czech VAT Act and § 435 of the Civil Code
For Slovak suppliers under § 74 of the Slovak VAT Act and § 3a of the Commercial Code
Supplier and customer name and address, company ID (IČO), VAT number and registry entry
Requires the customer's VAT number for reverse-charge invoices
Flags invoices with no lines, lines with no name or a zero quantity
For foreign customers, an extra e-invoice check against Peppol BIS 3.0 (EN 16931) rules
steps: Prepare a draft invoice as usual.
The invoice detail lists missing or incomplete details, each with the section of law it comes from.
Fill them in and issue the invoice.

faq.q: Does the check block issuing?
faq.a: No. It only warns – it separates errors from recommendations, but the decision is yours.

faq.q: Does it replace an accountant or tax adviser?
faq.a: No. It checks the formal requirements of the document, not whether the VAT rate or tax regime is right in your particular case.

faq.q: What is the Peppol check?
faq.a: For invoices abroad it verifies that the UBL e-invoice passes the main Peppol BIS 3.0 rules – for example that the customer has a VAT number and countries are filled in.

time.name: Time tracking
time.title: Time tracking and invoicing billable hours
time.description: Track project work with a timer or log it by hand. Billanta turns unbilled hours into a draft invoice at the project's rate in one click.
time.lead: Billing by the hour? The timer keeps running with the browser closed, and at month end you select the entries and click Invoice.
points: One-click timer, with the running time shown on the dashboard too
Manual entries with easy durations: 1:30, 1.5 or 90m
Projects with a customer, hourly rate, currency and colour
Override the rate on a single entry, or log non-billable work for the record
Invoice per project, per day or per entry – you get a draft to review
Invoiced entries are locked and link to their invoice; deleting the draft releases them
steps: Create a project with a customer and an hourly rate.
Start the timer or add work manually.
Select unbilled entries and choose how to merge them into invoice lines.
Review the draft and issue the invoice.

faq.q: Do I need a project?
faq.a: No. An entry can have no project – you then pick the customer when invoicing.

faq.q: How is the invoice quantity calculated?
faq.a: As hours worked, to three decimal places, with the unit “h”; the unit price is the project's or entry's rate.

faq.q: Can colleagues see my running timer?
faq.a: Each team member has their own timer. Entries and projects are shared across the company.

clientPortal.name: Client portal
clientPortal.title: Client portal – all of a customer's documents behind one link
clientPortal.description: Send each customer one permanent link showing all their invoices and quotes, what is left to pay and what is overdue. No sign-up, no password.
clientPortal.lead: Customers stop digging through old emails. One page lists their documents, each invoice with a payment QR and PDF.
points: One link per customer, turned on with a click in Contacts
Amount left to pay per currency, including the overdue part
Filters: all, to pay, paid, quotes
Each document opens with its payment QR, PDF and quote acceptance
Drafts and documents awaiting review are never shown
Renew or turn off the link at any time; the old one stops working
The link is added to invoice and reminder emails automatically, and templates get a {portal_link} variable
steps: Open the customer in Contacts and turn on the client portal.
Copy the link, or let the next invoice email carry it.
The customer opens the overview and pays by QR code.
Payments are matched from the bank statement and the portal updates right away.

faq.q: Does the customer need an account?
faq.a: No. The link itself grants access, so send it only to the customer. If it leaks, create a new one.

faq.q: Will the customer see internal notes?
faq.a: No. The portal shows only issued documents and their public details, never internal notes or drafts.

faq.q: Can search engines find the portal?
faq.a: No. The page is marked noindex and the link is not passed on in the Referer header.

companies.name: Multiple companies
companies.title: Several companies under one sign-in
companies.description: Invoice for your company and your sole-trader business from one account. Each company has its own documents, number series, team and settings, one click apart.
companies.lead: One sign-in, separate books for each company.
points: Add a company in Settings → My companies
Switch companies from the menu under your avatar
Data, number series, bank and backups stay separate
A different role in each company, e.g. owner here, accountant there
Accountants serve several clients without extra accounts
steps: Open Settings → My companies.
Enter the new company's name and accept the terms.
Fill in the company details and start invoicing.

faq.q: Is each company billed separately?
faq.a: Each company has its own plan. You can use the free plan for each of them.

faq.q: Can I move documents between companies?
faq.a: No, a document always belongs to one company. Each company also has its own contact list.

faq.q: How many companies can I have?
faq.a: Up to 10 as owner. Anyone can invite you to further companies through their team.

cardPayments.name: Card payments
cardPayments.title: Card payments straight from the invoice
cardPayments.description: Your client opens the invoice link and pays by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. The invoice is marked as paid and the gateway fee is recorded with the payment.
cardPayments.lead: Faster payments, no copying account numbers.
points: A "Pay by card" button on the invoice link
Money goes straight to your Stripe account, Billanta never holds it
The invoice is marked as paid automatically
Stripe's fee is recorded with the payment for margins and bookkeeping
A partly paid invoice asks only for the rest
The bank-transfer QR code stays next to the card option
steps: Create a restricted key for Checkout in Stripe.
Paste it in Settings → Payment methods → Card payments.
Send the invoice and your client pays by card from the link.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: Billanta charges nothing extra. You only pay Stripe's fees under your own Stripe pricing.

faq.q: When is the invoice marked as paid?
faq.a: As soon as the client returns from the payment page, and at the latest ten minutes after paying.

faq.q: Does Billanta see card details?
faq.a: No. The client enters the card only on Stripe's secure page.

taxEstimate.name: Tax and levy estimate
taxEstimate.title: What you keep from an invoice after tax and levies
taxEstimate.description: Each invoice shows a rough net amount after income tax and social and health insurance under Czech sole-trader rules. For the whole year we work out the tax, insurance and next year’s advances.
taxEstimate.lead: An invoice for CZK 20,000 does not mean CZK 20,000 in your account. Billanta shows you what you keep.
points: A "You keep" line on every invoice with a rough net amount
Works with a 60, 80, 40 or 30 % flat-rate expense, or none
Converted to CZK on foreign currency invoices
Yearly income tax estimate with the taxpayer credit
Social and health insurance, including next year’s advances
Enter the advances you paid and the estimate adjusts
steps: Issue an invoice and see right away what you keep.
Pick your flat rate, Billanta remembers it.
Open the yearly estimate in Exports, built from paid invoices and expenses.

faq.q: How accurate is it?
faq.a: It is a rough guide under Czech sole-trader rules. On an invoice it uses 15 % tax and insurance on that amount, without minimum advances or credits. The yearly estimate also counts the taxpayer credit and minimums, but it does not replace a tax return or a tax adviser.

faq.q: What is the yearly estimate based on?
faq.a: Paid invoices and recorded expenses for the chosen year. Expenses can be a flat rate or actual.

faq.q: Is it on the free plan?
faq.a: The "You keep" line on invoices is. The yearly estimate comes with the paid plans, from Start.

auditLog.lead: When something changes on an invoice, you know who, when and why. Even when it was AI or a system connected over the API.

The old and new value for each change
Author: a team member, AI, an API key or the system
An issued document can only be corrected with a stated reason
The whole company history in one place, under Activity
steps: Work as usual, the history records itself.
When correcting an issued document, give a reason.
Under Activity, see what changed in the company.

faq.q: Can a history entry be deleted or edited?
faq.a: No. The history is a record of what happened, so it cannot be edited in the app.

faq.q: Can my accountant see it?
faq.a: Company members see it according to their permissions, so an invited accountant does too if their role allows it.

items.a: Yes. You fill in the invoice and download it as a PDF with no sign-up, no email and no fee.

items.q: When is an account worth it?

brand.suitsUsTitle: When Billanta is the better pick

fakturoid.title: Billanta or Fakturoid?
fakturoid.lead: Fakturoid is a long-standing Czech invoicing app that many freelancers and accountants know. Billanta works on a different model: free with no customer limit, and AI included. Here is what that means for you.
suitsUs: You invoice more than five customers and don’t want to pay for a plan just for that.
You want to snap receipts or dictate an invoice into your phone without a paid add-on.
You need recurring invoices but not the top plan.
You do business in both Czechia and Slovakia, or send UBL (Peppol) e-invoices.
suitsThem: You want a native app from the App Store or Google Play rather than a web app on your home screen.
You connect your own system and need the API on the free plan.
Your accountant has worked with Fakturoid for years and switching wouldn’t save you anything.
fakturoid.price: Fakturoid’s free plan limits the number of customers; Billanta’s limits documents per month. If you bill a few regular clients, both free plans will do. If you have many small jobs for different people, Billanta costs less, because documents over the limit are paid one by one.
switchSteps: In Fakturoid, copy the API v3 Client ID and Client secret from your user account settings. Without the API, an export of invoices and contacts to CSV will do.

faq.q: Is Billanta cheaper than Fakturoid?
faq.a: Billanta’s cheapest paid plan, Start, is CZK 119 a month billed yearly (CZK 149 monthly); Fakturoid’s cheapest is CZK 151. Fakturoid’s free plan is capped at five customers, Billanta’s at ten documents a month with no customer limit. Both price lists are above, with the date we checked them.

faq.q: What do I get in Billanta for free?
faq.a: Ten documents a month with no customer limit, then CZK 5 each, so an occasional busy month doesn’t force a plan change. Two recurring invoices, QR payments, ISDOC, AI receipt reading and invoicing by voice (with a monthly limit) and the history import are free too. Bank payment matching and automatic reminders come with the paid plans.

faq.q: How do I move my data from Fakturoid?
faq.a: Two ways. Or upload an export of invoices and contacts to CSV or Excel, which the import recognises by its columns. Map any column it doesn’t know by hand in the preview.

faq.q: What comes over from Fakturoid?
faq.a: Customers with their company ID, VAT ID and address, issued invoices with dates, amounts, currency and payment status, and line items when the export has them. Without items, one line covers the whole amount. Customers you already have in Billanta are matched by company ID, otherwise by name, so nothing is duplicated. Your next invoice continues after the highest imported number, and if the old series used a different number format, the preview offers to keep it.

faq.q: Does anything change in my Fakturoid account?
faq.a: No. The import only reads your data; nothing in Fakturoid is changed or deleted. Over the API, Billanta only sends read requests and never stores your credentials. faq.a: Yes, on every plan including the free one. For each invoice you can download an ISDOC file for Czech accounting software and a UBL e-invoice in the Peppol BIS 3.0 format, which Slovak and other foreign customers ask for. Fakturoid’s price list includes ISDOC.

osvc.title: Czech sole trader (OSVČ) tax and insurance calculator
osvc.description: Get a rough figure for income tax, social and health insurance of a Czech sole trader (OSVČ) and next year's advances.
osvc.lead: Enter your income and expenses for the year. The calculator works out income tax, social and health insurance and the monthly advances you will pay next year.
osvc.keywords: income tax social health insurance advances flat expenses sole trader osvc czech
how: Profit is income minus actual expenses, or minus flat-rate expenses (a share of income, with a cap).
Income tax is 15 % of the profit rounded down to hundreds, and 23 % of the part above 36 times the average wage. The basic taxpayer credit is then deducted.
Social insurance is 29.2 % of 55 % of the profit, at least from the minimum and at most from the maximum assessment base.
Health insurance is 13.5 % of 50 % of the profit, at least from half the average wage for every month.
Next year's advances come from this year's base, but never below next year's minimum advances.

flatTax.conditionsTitle: Who can join the flat-rate regime
conditions: You are a sole trader (OSVČ) and not a VAT payer (an identified person is fine).
Business income stays under CZK 2,000,000 a year.

Band 1: income up to CZK 1,000,000 for any activity, up to CZK 1,500,000 if at least 75 % of income falls under the 80 % or 60 % flat-rate expenses, and up to CZK 2,000,000 if at least 75 % falls under the 80 % rate.
Band 2: up to CZK 1,500,000 for any activity and up to CZK 2,000,000 if at least 75 % of income falls under the 80 % or 60 % rate. Band 3: up to CZK 2,000,000.
You have no other income apart from small exceptions (for example a small salary, interest or rent within limits).
You are not a partner in a general partnership or a general partner in a limited partnership, and you are not insolvent.
You notify the tax office that you are joining by 10 January of that year.
how: The flat-rate tax is one monthly amount set by the band. The band depends on income and the main activity (§ 2a of the Czech Income Tax Act).

In the regular regime we deduct expenses (flat-rate up to the cap for the activity, or actual expenses), take the credits off the tax and calculate insurance from half the profit, at least from the minimum assessment base.
The child credit lowers the tax and what is left is paid out as a tax bonus. The bonus is paid from CZK 100 and only if income reaches six times the minimum wage (§ 35c).
This is an estimate for the whole year. Nothing is saved; the calculation runs in your browser.

vat.name: VAT calculator
vat.title: VAT calculator
vat.description: Add VAT to a net price or work it out from a gross price. Czech and Slovak rates.
vat.lead: Enter an amount and a rate. The calculator gives the base, the VAT and the price with VAT, both ways.
vat.keywords: vat rate 21 12 23 calculate vat net gross price czech slovak
how: From a net price: VAT = base × rate / 100, rounded to the cent.
From a gross price: base = price / (1 + rate / 100), and the VAT is the difference. The old Czech “coefficient” has not been used since 2019.
On an invoice, VAT is calculated for each rate separately. Rounding of the invoice total is handled at the end.

szco.name: Slovak sole trader tax
szco.title: Slovak sole trader (SZČO) tax and insurance calculator
szco.description: Get a rough figure for the income tax, health and social insurance of a Slovak sole trader (SZČO) for the year, with 60 % flat-rate expenses.
szco.lead: Enter your income for the year. The calculator works out Slovak personal income tax, health insurance, the social insurance due from July of the next year and the new health insurance advance.
szco.keywords: slovakia sole trader szco self-employed income tax flat-rate expenses social insurance health insurance allowance
how: Profit is income minus 60 % flat-rate expenses (at most EUR 20,000 a year) or minus actual expenses.
The tax base is profit minus the social and health insurance paid during the year. The taxpayer allowance is deducted; above an income threshold it gradually shrinks.
Tax is 15 % if income does not exceed EUR 100,000 (EUR 60,000 for 2024). Otherwise 19 % and 25 % on the part above 176.8 times the subsistence minimum, and from 2026 also 30 % and 35 %.
Health insurance is 15 % (16 % from 2026) of profit divided by 1.486, at least the minimum base for every month. The difference to the advances paid is settled in the yearly reconciliation.
Social insurance starts only in July of the next year, and only if income exceeds the legal threshold. The base is profit divided by 1.486 and by the months, between the minimum and the maximum base.

CZ.overviews: Annual statements for social and health insurance

CZ.vat_monthly: A monthly VAT payer files the VAT return and the control statement (kontrolní hlášení) by the 25th day after the month ends and pays the tax by the same day (§ 101 and § 101e of the Czech VAT Act).
CZ.vat_quarterly: A payer with last year's turnover up to CZK 15 million that is not an unreliable payer can file quarterly (§ 99a of the VAT Act). Return and payment by the 25th day after the quarter ends. Only individuals file the control statement quarterly; companies file it every month.
CZ.vat_other: Filings under special schemes (OSS, CESOP) follow the official calendar of the Czech Financial Administration.
CZ.vat_identified: An identified person files a return only for a month in which they had to self-assess VAT, typically after buying a service from abroad (ads, software), within 25 days after it ends (§ 101 of the VAT Act).
CZ.ec_sales_list: The EC sales list is filed by anyone who supplied goods or services to a business in another EU country that month, within 25 days after the month ends (§ 102 of the VAT Act).
CZ.health: A self-employed person's monthly health insurance advance is due by the 8th of the following month (§ 7 of Act No. 592/1992 Coll.).
CZ.social: A self-employed person's monthly social security advance is due by the 20th of the following month (§ 14a of Act No. 589/1992 Coll.).
CZ.income_tax: An electronic income tax return is filed and the tax paid by 1 May; since that is a public holiday, in practice the next working day. Paper returns by 1 April, with a tax advisor by 1 July (§ 136 of the Tax Code). Applies to sole traders and companies.
CZ.flat_tax: In the flat-rate regime (paušální režim) a single monthly payment replaces insurance advances and the tax return, due by the 20th of the month it covers (§ 2a and § 38lc of the Income Tax Act).
CZ.overviews: Self-employed people file annual statements (přehledy) with the Czech Social Security Administration and their health insurer within a month after the tax return deadline, so in early June with an electronic return.
CZ.payroll: An employer pays withheld income tax for the previous month by the 20th (§ 38h of the Income Tax Act). Employee insurance contributions are due on the same day.
CZ.road_tax: Road tax for the previous year is filed and paid by 31 January (Act No. 16/1993 Coll.).
CZ.property_tax: Property tax is due by 31 May; above CZK 5,000 it can be paid in two instalments (by 31 May and 30 November). A return is filed by 31 January only when something changed (Act No. 338/1992 Coll.).

SK.vat_monthly: A monthly VAT payer files the VAT return and the control statement (kontrolný výkaz) within 25 days after the month ends and pays the tax by the same day (§ 78 and § 78a of Act No. 222/2004 Coll.).
SK.vat_quarterly: A payer with lower turnover can have a quarterly tax period (§ 77 of the VAT Act). Return and control statement within 25 days after the quarter ends.
SK.vat_other: Filings under special schemes (OSS) follow the calendar of the Slovak Financial Administration.
SK.vat_identified: A person registered under § 7 or § 7a files a return only for a month in which they owed VAT, for example after buying a service from abroad, within 25 days after it ends.
SK.ec_sales_list: The EC sales list (súhrnný výkaz) is filed by anyone who supplied goods or services to a business in another EU country that month, within 25 days after the month ends (§ 80 of the VAT Act).
SK.health: A self-employed person's health insurance advance is due by the 8th of the following month (§ 24 of Act No. 580/2004 Coll.).
SK.social: A compulsorily insured self-employed person pays social insurance by the 8th of the month after the month it covers (§ 139 of Act No. 461/2003 Coll.).
SK.income_tax: The income tax return of individuals and companies is filed and the tax paid by 31 March. A notice extends it by 3 months, or by 6 months with foreign income (§ 49 of Act No. 595/2003 Coll.).
SK.flat_tax: The flat-rate regime is Czech; Slovakia has nothing like it.
SK.overviews: The annual statements are Czech; in Slovakia the Social Insurance Agency and health insurers work from the tax return.
SK.payroll: An employer pays withheld tax within 5 days after paying wages, so there is no fixed day in the month.
SK.road_tax: The motor vehicle tax return for the previous year is filed and the tax paid by 31 January (Act No. 361/2014 Coll.).
SK.property_tax: In Slovakia property tax is paid according to the municipality's decision, so there is no single fixed date.

vatReliability.name: Unreliable VAT payer check
vatReliability.title: Unreliable VAT payer check: Czech VAT ID and published bank account
vatReliability.description: Check for free whether a Czech supplier is an unreliable VAT payer and whether its bank account is published in the register of VAT payers. By VAT ID or company ID, straight from the Czech Financial Administration's register.
vatReliability.lead: Enter the supplier's Czech VAT ID (DIČ) or company ID (IČO) and, optionally, the account you are asked to pay. We check it in the Czech register of VAT payers.
vatReliability.keywords: unreliable vat payer czech check dic vat payer register czech published bank account vat liability supplier check
how: We ask the Czech Financial Administration's register of VAT payers directly. The result is valid at the moment of the check.

If you are a Czech VAT payer and the supplier is listed as unreliable on the taxable supply date or on the day you pay, you are liable for the VAT it doesn't pay (§ 109 of the Czech VAT Act). You avoid that by paying the VAT straight to its tax office (§ 109a of the VAT Act).
You are also liable when you pay for a supply to an account the payer has not published, whatever the amount (§ 109(2)(c) of the VAT Act).
We compare the account you enter with the published ones, whether you type it as a number with a bank code or as an IBAN. We don't show the list of published accounts, only how many there are.

how: ISDOC is the Czech e-invoice format. An .isdocx file is a zip holding the invoice plus a PDF and attachments – we unpack it for you.
We read the file in your browser only. Nothing is uploaded to a server and nothing stays once you close the page.

We check the company ID, VAT ID, bank account and IBAN checksums, the line and VAT totals, and the mandatory items for whoever issued the invoice. We don't look up VAT registration or the company in public registers.

vatFiling.name: VAT return, control and recapitulative statement
vatFiling.title: How to file the Czech VAT return, control statement and recapitulative statement
vatFiling.description: Who files the Czech VAT return, control statement (kontrolní hlášení) and recapitulative statement (souhrnné hlášení), the deadlines and how to file them online through EPO.
vatFiling.lead: A Czech VAT payer regularly files up to three reports with the tax office. Here is who files them, by when and how.
vatFiling.keywords: vat return control statement recapitulative statement dphdp3 dphkh1 dphshv epo deadline 25th czech
vatFiling.deadlinesNote: If the 25th falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deadline moves to the next working day.

sections.title: VAT return (DPHDP3)
sections.body: Every VAT payer files it for every tax period, even with no invoices. The tax period is a month, or a quarter if your turnover in the previous year did not exceed CZK 15 million, you are not an unreliable payer or part of a VAT group, and you choose quarterly filing. The return is filed and the tax paid by the 25th day after the period ends.

sections.title: Control statement (DPHKH1)
sections.body: Filed by payers who made or received domestic supplies in the period. Legal entities (such as an s.r.o.) always file it monthly by the 25th of the following month; individuals file it with the same deadline as their return, so quarterly filers file quarterly. Documents over CZK 10,000 including VAT are listed one by one (sections A.4 and B.2), smaller ones as totals. It can only be filed electronically, and late filing carries fixed fines starting at CZK 1,000.

sections.title: Recapitulative statement (DPHSHV)
sections.body: Filed for each month in which you supplied goods or services under reverse charge to a business in another EU country. The deadline is 25 days after the month ends. If you only supply services you may file it quarterly. Identified persons who supplied a service to the EU file it too.

sections.title: Filing online
sections.body: The return and the statements are filed electronically as XML. Most people upload the file to the Moje daně portal (the EPO application), check it and send it through their data box or with a qualified electronic signature. Pay the tax to your tax office's account with your tax ID without the CZ prefix as the variable symbol.

steps: Make sure you have every issued and received invoice for the period and that the tax point dates are right.
Create the XML files. In Billanta they are under Settings → Exports → VAT.
On the Moje daně portal open EPO, choose to load a file and upload the XML.
Fill in the tax office and any details the export leaves blank, then run the check.
Send the filing through your data box or with an electronic signature and keep the confirmation.
Pay the tax by the 25th day after the period ends.
before: Convert foreign-currency invoices at the ČNB rate of the day the tax became due.
For received invoices in the control statement you need the supplier's VAT number and the invoice number.
Corrective tax documents (credit notes) belong to the period in which you issued or received them.
Services bought from abroad under reverse charge are declared as output tax and, as a payer, you can claim them back as input tax.
vatFiling.formsLine: Forms described: DPHDP3 version {dp3}, DPHKH1 version {kh1}, DPHSHV version {shv}.

identified.name: Identified person for Czech VAT
identified.title: Identified person for Czech VAT: when you become one and what to file
identified.description: A Czech business that is not a VAT payer becomes an identified person when it buys ads or services from abroad or sells services to the EU. What that means and what to file.
identified.lead: Even if you are not a VAT payer, you can become an identified person (identifikovaná osoba). Paying for Facebook or Google ads is usually enough. You then have to declare and pay Czech VAT on that purchase.
identified.keywords: identified person vat reverse charge facebook google ads services from abroad registration 15 days czech

sections.title: Who is an identified person
sections.body: A business that is not a VAT payer but has to register for VAT because of cross-border deals. You become one mainly when you:

sections.title: Buying ads and services from abroad
sections.body: Google Ads, Facebook and Instagram ads, software subscriptions or other services from a foreign supplier: the place of supply is Czechia because you are a business. The supplier invoices you without VAT and you declare and pay the tax yourself (usually 21 %). This is called reverse charge. As an identified person you cannot claim this VAT back, so it is a real cost for you.

sections.title: What to file and when
sections.body: You file a VAT return only for the months in which tax became due, by the 25th of the following month, and pay the tax by the same date. If you supplied a service to a business in another EU country, you also file a recapitulative statement for that month. Identified persons do not file the control statement. Everything is filed electronically.

sections.title: When you become a VAT payer
sections.body: An identified person is still not a VAT payer. You become one once your turnover for a calendar year exceeds CZK 2,000,000, from 1 January of the next year. If it exceeds CZK 2,536,500 during the year, you become a payer the very next day.

who: receive a service from a foreign supplier (for example ads from Google or Meta),
supply a service to a business in another EU country,
buy goods from another EU country for more than CZK 326,000 in a calendar year.
identified.registration: File the registration with your tax office within 15 days of becoming an identified person. You get a VAT number (DIČ), which you then give to foreign suppliers so they invoice you without VAT.
identified.example: In March you pay CZK 10,000 for Facebook ads. Meta invoices you without VAT. By 25 April you file a VAT return for March showing tax of CZK 2,100 and pay the same amount to the tax office. In months without such purchases you file nothing.

skEinvoicing.name: E-invoicing in Slovakia 2027
skEinvoicing.title: E-invoicing in Slovakia from 2027: who must comply, when and how to prepare
skEinvoicing.description: From 1 January 2027 Slovak VAT payers must send domestic B2B invoices as e-invoices over Peppol, and every Slovak business must be able to receive them. Dates, exemptions, penalties and a checklist.
skEinvoicing.lead: From 1 January 2027 a PDF invoice sent by email is no longer enough in Slovakia. VAT payers will send structured e-invoices to businesses through a certified provider, and every business must be able to receive them, VAT-registered or not. A summary based on the Slovak VAT Act and the Slovak Financial Administration's guidance.
skEinvoicing.keywords: slovakia e-invoicing 2027 mandatory e-invoicing slovakia peppol act 385/2025 § 85o certified provider 0245 dic slovak vat e-invoice

timeline.text: Voluntary phase. You can already send e-invoices through a certified provider if the buyer has one too. Nothing is mandatory yet.
Mandatory domestic phase. Slovak VAT payers must issue e-invoices within 15 days for supplies made from this day, and every business and legal person in Slovakia must be able to receive them.
Second phase under the EU ViDA directive: e-invoices for intra-EU supplies too, the deadline drops to 10 days, and the Slovak control statement and recapitulative statement are abolished.

issuers: a Slovak VAT payer (registered under § 4, 4b or 4c of the Slovak VAT Act),
for a supply of goods or services whose place of supply is Slovakia,
to another taxable person (a company or sole trader, VAT-registered or not) or a legal person such as a municipality or an association.
This covers invoices, credit notes, debit notes and invoices for advance payments received.
skEinvoicing.receiveLabel: Must be able to receive e-invoices:
skEinvoicing.receivers: every business and every legal person in Slovakia, even if it is not VAT-registered. In practice that means a contract with a certified provider from 1 January 2027. The buyer's consent is not needed when the e-invoice is mandatory.
outside: supplies exempt under § 28 to 43 and § 47 (such as financial and insurance services),
sales documented by an eKasa till receipt up to €400 or a simplified invoice up to €100,
supplies within a VAT group and classified supplies,
a proforma invoice, which is not a tax document.
skEinvoicing.czNote: A Czech company that is not VAT-registered in Slovakia does not have to issue Slovak e-invoices until 30 June 2030. If you are VAT-registered in Slovakia, ask a tax adviser whether the mandate applies to you.
skEinvoicing.howBody: An e-invoice is not a PDF or a scan. It is an XML file in the Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 format (European standard EN 16931). It is not emailed or uploaded to a government portal but delivered over the Peppol network:
howSteps: You sign up with a certified delivery provider. The Slovak Financial Administration listed 80 of them on 16 October 2026 and estimates a simple plan at €5 – 12 a month.
Your address on the network is 0245:DIČ, your Slovak tax number with the prefix 0245.
Your invoicing software creates the XML and hands it to your provider, which delivers it to the buyer's provider.
The providers report the invoice data to the tax administration automatically: the supplier's on issue, the buyer's within 5 days of receipt.
skEinvoicing.corrections: You correct an invoice with a credit note (e-invoice type 381) that references the original invoice, plus a new invoice if needed. Type 384 (corrected invoice) is not used in Slovakia yet. An invoice for an advance payment received is a tax document and goes out as an e-invoice with code 388. A proforma invoice is not a tax document.
skEinvoicing.penalties: For not reporting the data, or reporting it late or wrongly, the tax office can impose a fine of up to €10,000, or up to €100,000 for a repeated breach. An obvious mistake corrected promptly, or a proven outage at the provider, is not fined.
skEinvoicing.pending: An amendment before the Slovak parliament would add a period without fines from 1 January to 30 June 2027 and drop the buyer's reporting of received invoices. Until parliament passes it, the rules above apply.
checklist: Find out whether you are a Slovak VAT payer and who you invoice. The check below helps.
Pick a certified provider from the Financial Administration's list and compare prices.
Make sure your invoicing software can produce Peppol BIS 3.0 XML and pass it to the provider.
Add the IČO and DIČ to your customers. Without the DIČ the e-invoice cannot be delivered.
Agree with your accountant how incoming e-invoices will be received and booked.
Update how you handle corrections (credit note 381) and advance payment invoices (388).
Try sending in 2026 while the phase is still voluntary.
Set up 10-year archiving of the XML files.

skEinvoicing.checkLead: Answer a few questions. The result is for an ordinary invoice from 1 January 2027.

result.mandatory: From 1 January 2027 you must send these customers e-invoices over Peppol, within 15 days of the supply.
result.nonPayer: As a non-VAT payer you do not have to issue e-invoices. You can if you want to.
result.exempt: The mandate does not cover exempt supplies. If you also make taxable supplies, it applies to those.
result.noB2b: You do not have to send e-invoices to private individuals. If you also invoice businesses, those invoices are covered.

Delivery and reporting status on every invoice.

faq.q: Can I still email a PDF invoice from 2027?
faq.a: Not for an invoice the mandate covers. A PDF or a scan is not an e-invoice. The tax document is the Peppol BIS 3.0 XML delivered through a certified provider. You can send a PDF as well, as a readable copy.

faq.q: I am not VAT-registered. Do I need to do anything?
faq.a: If you do business in Slovakia, yes, but only receive. From 1 January 2027 every business and legal person in Slovakia must be able to receive e-invoices, so you need a certified provider. You do not have to issue them.

faq.q: Do I need the buyer's consent?
faq.a: No. When the e-invoice is mandatory, the buyer's consent is not required.

faq.q: Is the e-invoice sent to a tax administration portal?
faq.a: No. It goes from your provider to the buyer's provider over the Peppol network. The providers send selected invoice data to the tax administration automatically.

faq.q: Does it apply to Czech companies invoicing Slovak customers?
faq.a: Cross-border invoices are outside the mandate until 30 June 2030, so a Czech company without Slovak VAT registration does not have to issue them. From 1 July 2030 e-invoicing extends to trade within the EU.

faq.q: Has the start been postponed?
faq.a: No. The 1 January 2027 date stands. An amendment in the Slovak parliament (print 1454) only proposes a six-month period without fines, and it had not been passed as of 19 October 2026.

supplierName.label: Supplier's name or business name
supplierName.hint: Exactly as in the business or trade register.

supplierAddress.label: Supplier's registered address
supplierAddress.hint: The registered seat, not just a mailing address.

supplierIco.label: Supplier's company ID (IČO)
supplierIco.hint: Eight digits; we verify the check digit.

supplierRegistry.label: Register entry
supplierRegistry.hint: E.g. “Registered in the Commercial Register at the Municipal Court in Prague, section C, file 123”. A sole trader only in the trade register can leave it out in Czechia.

supplierDic.label: Supplier's VAT ID
supplierDic.hint: With the country prefix, e.g. CZ or SK.

customerName.label: Customer's name or business name
customerName.hint: For a consumer the name is enough.

customerIco.label: Customer's company ID
customerIco.hint: The law doesn't ask for it, but businesses want it for their books.

customerDic.label: Customer's VAT ID
customerDic.hint: With the country prefix, e.g. CZ12345678 or DE123456789.

documentLabel.label: Document title
documentLabel.hint: So it is clear what kind of document it is.

number.label: Document number
number.hint: Unique within your numbering series; it must never repeat.

originalNumber.label: Number of the corrected invoice
originalNumber.hint: The number of the original invoice the credit note corrects.

issueDate.label: Issue date
issueDate.hint: The day you issued the document.

taxPointDate.label: Date of supply (tax point)
taxPointDate.hint: When you delivered the goods or provided the service.

subject.label: What and how much was supplied

unitPrice.label: Unit price excluding VAT
unitPrice.hint: Price per piece, hour or other unit, plus any discount not already in the price.

vatRate.label: VAT rate
vatRate.hint: The rate that applies, or 0 % for an exempt supply.

total.label: Total to pay
total.hint: How much the customer should pay.

correctionReason.label: Reason for the correction
correctionReason.hint: E.g. returned goods, a discount, a wrong price.

correctionDifference.label: Change in tax base and VAT
correctionDifference.hint: By how much the base and the VAT change against the original invoice (with a minus sign).

reverseChargeNote.label: Reverse-charge note
reverseChargeNote.hint: “Daň odvede zákazník” (CZ) or “prenesenie daňovej povinnosti” (SK), or “Reverse charge” for an EU customer. The customer accounts for the VAT.

exemptionNote.label: Reference to the VAT exemption
exemptionNote.hint: E.g. “Exempt under § 64 of the VAT act”, or a reference to the VAT directive.

nonPayerNote.label: “Not a VAT payer” note
nonPayerNote.hint: Not required by law, but the customer immediately knows why there's no VAT.

dueDate.label: Due date
dueDate.hint: Without it the statutory term applies and a reminder is harder to argue.

paymentDetails.label: Bank account and payment reference
paymentDetails.hint: Ideally with a payment QR code so the customer pays without retyping.

notes.ifRegistered: Only if you are entered in the commercial or another public register.
notes.ifDifferent: Only if it differs from the issue date.
notes.buyerVatId: The VAT ID from another EU state (check it in VIES).
notes.inHomeCurrency: In the home currency (CZK or EUR) even if you invoice in another currency.
notes.noVatAmountReverse: For information only – you don't calculate the VAT, the customer does.
notes.totalOrBase: The total including VAT, or the base and the VAT separately.
notes.proformaLabel: E.g. “Pro forma invoice – not a tax document”.
notes.exemptEuGoods: Supplying goods to the EU is exempt from VAT.
notes.exportOrAbroad: For exported goods or a service supplied outside the EU.

faq.q: How much does Billanta cost for an accounting firm?
faq.a: Signing up and joining the programme are free. From the Start plan up, access to a client’s company is included in the client’s plan. Credits for paying clients can pay for your own firm’s plan.

faq.q: Is Billanta for tax advisers too?
faq.a: Yes. A tax adviser joins a client’s company the same way an accountant does, with the accountant role, and gets the same exports and reports, including the income tax summary. The partner programme and the town page listing work the same way.

faq.a: The client invites your email with the accountant role in Settings → Team. Once you accept, their company shows up in the company switcher in your account.

faq.q: Which exports does Billanta support?
faq.a: Czech VAT return, control statement and EC sales list for the EPO portal, the Slovak VAT return, control statement and EC sales list for eDane, ISDOC invoices, exports for Pohoda and Money S3, and CSV.

faq.q: How do I get onto the town pages?
faq.a: In Settings → Accountant profile, fill in your directory listing with the region you work in and send it. We review every listing by hand. Once approved, your firm shows up in the accountant directory and on the town pages in your region, usually within an hour.

faq.q: How many credits do I get?
faq.a: The same as a normal referral, partner programme or not: the client gets {welcome} credits when signing up through your link. You get as many credits as the client pays in CZK for the first plan payment, up to {reward}. On a monthly plan we add them after the second payment, on a yearly one 30 days after payment. If the client gets a refund or cancels before that, there is no reward. 1 credit = CZK 1.

faq.q: Do I need to sign up or give an e-mail for the demo?
faq.a: No. Pick a kind of company and you are in the app in a few seconds. No e-mail, password or card.

faq.q: How long does the demo last?
faq.a: The sample company lasts 24 hours. Then it is deleted along with everything you created in it.

faq.q: Can I try the accountant's or a colleague's view?
faq.a: Yes. In the demo's top bar you switch between the owner, the accountant and a read-only colleague. Each role has the same permissions as in a real company.

faq.q: Can I start with an empty company?
faq.a: Yes. Pick an empty company when starting, or use "start with an empty company" in the demo bar. You get a company with no documents and create everything yourself.

faq.q: Will invoices from the demo move into my account?
faq.a: Yes, if you create the account straight from the demo. After signing up we offer to move the invoices, contacts and expenses you created. Invoices arrive as drafts, so you issue them under your own details and numbering.

faq.q: Does anything from the demo reach real people?
faq.a: No. The demo sends no e-mails, connects no bank and charges nothing. All companies and people in it are made up.

shareQr.lead: Scan the QR code with a phone, or download it for a poster or a slide.
shareQr.promoHint: With a code, the QR leads to the page for joining a group, such as an event or a coworking. We issue the codes, so a made-up one will not work.
