schools.seoTitle: Billanta for schools – free invoicing for teaching
schools.title: Invoicing your students actually get to try
schools.lead: Billanta is free for teaching. On practice companies, students go through the whole life of an invoice: issuing it, correcting it, chasing it and billing a foreign customer, under both Czech and Slovak rules.
schools.practiceLead: The same steps every freelancer and every bookkeeper takes, without the risk of breaking anything real.

vatInvoice.title: VAT invoice
vatInvoice.body: Required fields, VAT rates, the date of the taxable supply and why they matter. The required-fields check shows straight away what is missing.

creditNote.title: Credit note
creditNote.body: A discount after issuing, returned goods or a wrong price. Students see how the original invoice is corrected and what that changes for VAT.

reminder.title: Reminder and payment
reminder.body: An overdue invoice, a reminder, a partial payment and matching it. A piece of practice school rarely gets to.

foreign.title: Foreign customer
foreign.body: An invoice in euros, the central bank rate, reverse charge and a bilingual document for a customer from another EU country.

czsk.title: Czech vs. Slovak rules
czsk.body: The same invoice under Czech and Slovak rules: different VAT rates and different tax IDs.

roles.title: Owner and teacher
roles.body: Who may see and change what. Each student runs their company as the owner, and the teacher can look in read-only. An exercise with accountant access is in the works.

access.title: How to get Billanta for your class
access.lead: We are finishing a classroom mode. Teachers who get in touch now will be among the first to have it.

request.title: Write to us
request.body: The school, the subject, the year and roughly how many students. We can verify you faster from a school email.

setup.title: We set up the class
setup.body: You get teacher access and practice companies for the students to work on. Soon you will create them yourself.

teach.title: You teach
teach.body: Students issue documents on their practice companies, and you see their work and can go through it with them.

access.soon: Until then you can show your students the no-signup demo on the projector.

schools.safeguardsTitle: A practice environment, not a real business

practice.title: Practice companies
practice.body: Students work on made-up companies and customers. They do not need to enter any real personal data.

watermark.title: Watermarked documents
watermark.body: Documents from the classroom mode will carry a visible practice mark, so nobody mistakes them for a real invoice.

notReal.title: For teaching only
notReal.body: Teaching access is not meant for a real business. Anyone who starts invoicing for real opens a regular account.

schools.privacyLink: A short <link>privacy notice for pupils and parents</link> explains what is stored about pupils and who can see it.
schools.resourcesLead: Lessons and worksheets, guides to the legislation and pages that explain each topic in detail.

resources.firstInvoice: Your first invoice: what it must contain

faq.q: Is Billanta for schools really free?
faq.a: Yes. The school, the teacher and the students pay nothing for teaching. Only a regular account for a real business is paid.

faq.q: Which schools is teaching access for?
faq.a: Primary and secondary schools, especially business academies and schools with economics subjects, colleges and universities, and retraining courses. If you teach invoicing elsewhere, write to us too.

faq.q: When will the classroom mode be ready?
faq.a: Soon. Teachers who request access now get it among the first and can tell us what they need in class.

faq.q: Can students use Billanta for their own business?
faq.a: Not with teaching access, which is for practice only. For real invoicing a student opens a regular account that works independently of the school.

faq.q: What about students’ personal data?
faq.a: Practice does not need any. Pupils join a class with only the class code and a nickname, without an email or password. The companies and customers are made up, and practice companies are deleted 30 days after the class ends.

creators.seoTitle: Invoicing for creators and influencers – brands, agencies, euros
creators.title: Invoice brand deals without the headache
creators.lead: A campaign for a brand, a fee from an agency, a payout from a platform abroad. Billanta issues the invoice in crowns or euros, handles reverse charge and reminds clients who have not paid.

brands.title: Brands and agencies
brands.body: One invoice per campaign or per deliverable. The line items say exactly what you deliver: the number of posts or videos, a licence to use the content.

eur.title: Invoices in euros
eur.body: Invoice in EUR and other currencies. The central bank rate fills in by itself, and the invoice shows the converted amount too.

reverseCharge.title: Reverse charge
reverseCharge.body: A business in another EU country usually accounts for the VAT itself. The invoice then carries the customer’s VAT ID and a reverse-charge note. A non-VAT payer often has to register for VAT purposes because of it.

abroad.title: Clients outside the EU
abroad.body: A deal with a US brand or platform: an invoice in English, in dollars or euros, with the right wording on the place of supply.

advance.title: Advances and quotes
advance.body: Send a quote, get an advance paid and issue the final invoice after the campaign. All in one place and linked together.

recurring.title: Ongoing deals
recurring.body: An ambassador contract with a monthly fee? A recurring invoice is issued and sent by itself.

flatTax.title: Flat tax and flat-rate expenses
flatTax.body: Most creators are self-employed and use a flat-rate regime. Billanta shows how much you have invoiced this year, so you know where you stand against the limits.
points: In Czechia, the flat tax: one monthly payment for income tax and insurance, if you are not a VAT payer and stay under the income limit.
Or flat-rate expenses as a percentage of income, with an estimate of tax and insurance in the app.
In Slovakia, flat-rate expenses and an estimate of tax and contributions for the self-employed.
Always check your own situation with an accountant, who can see your invoicing data straight from Billanta.

partner.title: Want your own code for your audience?
partner.body: We work with creators who talk to their followers about business and money. Your audience gets a perk when signing up, and you see how many people used your code.
points: We issue the code after a short chat.
We agree the perk for your followers and the terms together.
And yes, you can invoice us for the collaboration from Billanta.
You must clearly label paid and partner posts as advertising or a collaboration.

faq.q: Do I have to be a VAT payer to invoice foreign companies?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A non-VAT payer who supplies services to a business in another EU country usually has to register for VAT purposes and file EC sales lists, though. Billanta puts the right note on the invoice, but the registration and filings are for you and your accountant or tax office.

faq.q: Can I invoice a Czech agency in euros?
faq.a: Yes, if you agree on it. Billanta fills in the central bank rate and the amount in crowns needed for tax.

faq.q: What if a brand pays me in products instead of money?
faq.a: A barter deal is usually taxable income too. How to account for it depends on the deal, so ask your accountant. You then issue the document in Billanta like any other invoice.

faq.q: How do I get a promo code for my followers?
faq.a: Write to us. We issue the codes ourselves once we agree on the terms, and then you just share them, for example as a QR code from this page.

events.seoTitle: Billanta for meetups, coworkings and communities
events.title: Let your attendees try invoicing on the spot
events.lead: Running a meetup, a course for new founders or a coworking space? We will prepare a code and a QR code for your attendees. They try Billanta in 30 seconds, without signing up.

code.title: A code for attendees
code.body: A perk when they sign up, such as a few months for free. We agree the terms for each event.

qr.title: A QR code for posters and slides
qr.body: Download it as PNG or SVG and print it at any size. The code is already in the link.

demo.title: A demo in 30 seconds
demo.body: Attendees scan the QR code and land in a sample company with invoices, payments and VAT. No e-mail, no password.

write.title: Write to us
write.body: When and where the event is, how many people you expect and who they are.

print.title: We send the code
print.body: You get the code and a QR code. You can also draw the same QR here with the Share button.

scan.title: Attendees scan
scan.body: Anyone can try the demo right there. Those who want to stay sign up with your code.

contact.title: Let’s talk
contact.body: It is free for organisers. A few lines about your event are enough and we will get back with a proposal.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: Nothing for organisers. We prepare the attendee code and the QR code for free.

faq.q: Do attendees need to install anything?
faq.a: No. The demo runs in the browser on a phone or a computer and needs no signup.

faq.q: What exactly do attendees get with the code?
faq.a: A perk when signing up that we agree on, such as a few months for free. They enter the code at signup, or it is already in the link from the QR code.

coworking.title: For coworkings: one QR code for all members
coworking.body: A coworking does not need an event, a standing code is enough. Put the QR code up at the reception or in the kitchen, or tell members the passphrase.
points: One permanent QR code or passphrase for all members.
They scan it and they are in. You never create accounts one by one.
For members who stay with Billanta, the coworking can earn referral credits.

how.title: How it works for partners
how.lead: No lists of names, no accounts created one by one. Your people sign up themselves, with your benefit already applied.

code.title: We issue your code
code.body: One group code with the benefit we agree on: a free period, a discount or extra credit.

share.title: You get a QR, a poster and a link
share.body: Print the poster, put the QR on a slide or paste the link into your newsletter or group chat.

scan.title: Members scan and are in
scan.body: Each person opens the link, sets up their own company and starts invoicing. They can try the demo first, without signing up.

track.title: You see sign-ups and earn credit
track.body: You see how many people joined through your code and get credit for each one who starts paying (by default up to {reward} credits, based on the first payment, 1 credit = CZK 1).

contact.title: Let's set it up
contact.body: Write a few lines about your group and how many people it has. We reply within two working days with a code and a suggested benefit.

hub.title: Bring Billanta to your people
hub.seoTitle: Partner programmes – courses, coworkings, communities, banks
hub.lead: Courses, coworkings, communities, schools, creators, accountants and banks: each gets one code for its whole group, a benefit for members and credit for every company that starts paying.

courses.title: Business start-up courses
courses.body: Retraining and start-up courses, incubators. Participants invoice for free while the course runs.

coworkings.title: Coworkings
coworkings.body: One permanent QR for all members, a poster for the wall and credit for the space.

communities.title: Communities and associations
communities.body: Associations of the self-employed, unions, Facebook and Discord groups. A member code and an optional talk.

expats.title: Expats and digital nomads
expats.body: Invoices in English, EUR and CZK, reverse charge. For relocation agencies and expat groups.

schools.title: Schools
schools.body: Lessons on invoicing and running a business, with a classroom demo.

creators.title: Creators
creators.body: Your own code for your audience and credit for every company that stays.

events.title: Events and fairs
events.body: A code for the attendees of a conference, fair or meetup.

accountants.title: Accountants
accountants.body: A listing in the accountant directory, access to your clients’ companies and exports.

banks.title: Banks
banks.body: An offer for business-account clients, bank sync and co-branded codes.

courses.title: Your participants are starting a business. Their invoicing can start in the lesson.
courses.seoTitle: Invoicing for business start-up courses and incubators
courses.lead: For retraining courses from the labour office, start-up programmes such as CzechInvest's and incubators. Participants issue their first invoice during the course, free of charge, with a code you hand out in the first session.

free.title: Free while the course runs
free.body: Participants use the paid plan for free for the length of the course and a bit beyond, so the first real invoices are covered too.

code.title: One code for the whole group
code.body: A single QR or passphrase for each run of the course. Nobody has to collect e-mails or create accounts.

lessons.title: Ready-made lessons
lessons.body: Short lessons on invoicing, VAT and payments that lecturers can use as they are or pick parts from.

empty.title: A "just founded" start
empty.body: The demo opens as an empty new business: no sample documents, just the settings a beginner needs.

noAccounts.title: Each person sets up their own company
noAccounts.body: Participants enter their own ID number and bank account. The data belongs to them, not to the course.

lecturer.title: Help for lecturers
lecturer.body: We gladly walk your lecturers through the app before the first run, online, in about half an hour.

lesson.title: A lesson that ends with a real invoice
lesson.lead: A simple outline that fits into one session:
points: What a valid invoice must contain and why
Setting up the new business: ID number, address, bank account
Issuing a first invoice with a QR payment code
Recording a payment and sending a polite reminder
What the accountant or the tax office will want at year end

faq.q: Who can use the course offer?
faq.a: Any course that helps people start a business: retraining courses, start-up programmes, incubators and accelerators. Write to us and we set up a code for your next run.

faq.q: What happens when the free period ends?
faq.a: Participants can stay on the free plan or pick a paid one. Nothing is charged automatically and nobody loses their invoices.

faq.q: Can participants practise without a real business yet?
faq.a: Yes. The empty demo works without signing up, and a demo company can later be moved to a real account.

faq.q: Does the course see participants' invoices?
faq.a: No. The course only sees how many people joined through its code. Each company's data stays private.

courses.contactTitle: Get a code for your next course
courses.contactBody: Tell us when the course starts and how many participants it has. We send the code, a poster and the lessons ahead of the first session.

coworkings.title: One QR on the wall, a benefit for every member
coworkings.lead: Most coworking members are freelancers who invoice every month. Give them a better start in Billanta as part of the membership, with one permanent code that never needs updating.

permanent.title: A permanent code
permanent.body: One QR and passphrase for all members, now and later. New members simply use the same one.

benefit.title: A member benefit
benefit.body: A free period or a discount on the paid plan, which you can list among your membership perks.

credit.title: Credit for the coworking
credit.body: For each member company that starts paying, the coworking gets credit (by default up to {reward} credits, based on the first payment). Larger arrangements we agree individually.

poster.title: A poster for the wall
poster.body: A printable A4 or A3 poster with your code, for the kitchen, the reception or the meeting room.

qr.title: A QR for screens and chats
qr.body: The same code works on a lobby screen, in your newsletter or in the members' group chat.

members.title: No admin work for you
members.body: Members sign up themselves. You don't manage accounts, licences or departures.

faq.q: Does the code ever expire?
faq.a: No, a coworking code is permanent unless you ask us to change it. Posters you print today keep working.

faq.q: Do we need to use Billanta ourselves?
faq.a: No. The credit can go towards your own subscription if you use it, and for larger communities we agree a different reward.

faq.q: Can we see who signed up?
faq.a: You see the number of sign-ups and paying companies, not their names or invoices.

coworkings.contactTitle: Get a code for your coworking
coworkings.contactBody: Tell us the name of the space and roughly how many members it has. We send the code and a poster to print.

communities.title: A member benefit your community will actually use
communities.seoTitle: Invoicing benefit for associations and freelancer communities
communities.lead: For associations of the self-employed, trade unions and professional groups, and for Facebook or Discord communities of freelancers. One member code, an optional talk on invoicing and credit for the community.

code.title: A member code
code.body: One code for all members, which you share in your newsletter, member zone or a pinned post.

benefit.title: A benefit for members
benefit.body: A free period or a discount on the paid plan, a concrete perk you can name in your offer.

talk.title: A talk or webinar (optional)
talk.body: A short, practical session on invoicing, VAT deadlines and getting paid on time. No sales pitch.

credit.title: Credit for the community
credit.body: For each member company that starts paying, the community earns credit (by default up to {reward} credits, based on the first payment).

online.title: Made for online groups
online.body: A link and a QR that work in a post, a chat or a stream. Members can try the demo first, without signing up.

members.title: Members stay independent
members.body: Every member has their own company and data. The community does not manage anyone's account.

faq.q: Is there a minimum group size?
faq.a: No. A local association with thirty members is as welcome as a group of thousands.

faq.q: What does the talk cover?
faq.a: Whatever your members need: a first invoice, VAT registration thresholds, reminders, working with an accountant. About 30 to 45 minutes, online or in person.

faq.q: Can we see what our members invoice?
faq.a: No. You only see how many members joined and how many pay. Their companies stay private.

communities.contactBody: Tell us about your community and whether you would like a talk. We send the code, a QR and a short text for your members.

expats.title: Invoicing in Czechia and Slovakia, in English
expats.seoTitle: Invoicing for expats and freelancers in Czechia and Slovakia
expats.lead: For foreigners who run a trade licence or a company in Czechia or Slovakia, and for the relocation agencies, expat groups and coworkings that help them. The app and the invoices speak English; the rules are the local ones.

english.title: The app and invoices in English
english.body: Use the whole app in English and issue invoices in English, or in two languages side by side.

currencies.title: EUR, CZK and other currencies
currencies.body: Invoice in euros or any other currency. The VAT in Czech crowns is added from the Czech National Bank rate.

reverseCharge.title: Reverse charge for EU clients
reverseCharge.body: Invoices to VAT payers in other EU countries carry the right note and leave the VAT to the client.

checks.title: Checks before you send
checks.body: The app warns you when something the law requires is missing, so a Czech accountant won't send the invoice back.

recurring.title: Recurring invoices
recurring.body: A monthly retainer for a foreign client goes out on its own, with a QR code for local clients.

remote.title: Works from anywhere
remote.body: In the browser and on your phone, from Prague, Bratislava or anywhere else.

musts.title: What a Czech or Slovak invoice must contain
musts.lead: The short version, for a freelancer or a small company:
points: Your name or company name, address and company ID (IČO)
The client's name and address, and their ID and VAT number if they have one
A unique invoice number, the date of issue and the due date
What you supplied, the quantity and the price
If you are a VAT payer: your VAT number, the date of the taxable supply, the rate and the VAT amount, in CZK in Czechia and in EUR in Slovakia
If you are not a VAT payer, it's good practice to say so on the invoice
For a VAT-registered EU client: both VAT numbers and the reverse charge note
musts.note: A summary, not tax advice. The details depend on your situation; the guides below go further.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Czech or Slovak to use it?
faq.a: No. The app, the invoices, the e-mails to clients and the help are available in English.

faq.q: Can I invoice in euros from Czechia?
faq.a: Yes. You can invoice in EUR or another currency. If you are a Czech VAT payer, the VAT amount is also shown in CZK, which the app fills in from the Czech National Bank rate.

faq.q: My client is a company in Germany. What changes?
faq.a: If they are a VAT payer, the invoice usually goes without Czech VAT under the reverse charge, with both VAT numbers on it. You may also need to file a recapitulative statement.

faq.q: We help expats relocate. Can we offer this to our clients?
faq.a: Yes. We issue a code for your clients with a benefit, and you earn credit for every company that starts paying.

expats.contactBody: Relocation agencies, expat communities and coworkings get a code for their clients or members. Write to us in English, Czech or Slovak.

banks.title: Invoicing for your business-account clients
banks.seoTitle: Partnership for banks – invoicing for business clients
banks.lead: Small businesses open an account with you and then look for a way to invoice. Offer them Billanta as part of the account: invoices with your account number and QR payment, payments paired automatically and a co-branded code.

clients.title: An offer for new business accounts
clients.body: A free period or a discount for clients who open a business account, handed out in your app, branch or welcome e-mail.

sync.title: Bank sync and payment pairing
sync.body: Incoming payments are paired with invoices automatically, so your clients see what is paid without exporting statements.

cobranded.title: Co-branded codes
cobranded.body: A code and a landing page carrying both brands, with the benefit you choose for your clients.

onboarding.title: A quick start for new businesses
onboarding.body: Many new account holders are founding a business. They get a ready invoice with your account and QR code in minutes.

api.title: Integration
api.body: An API and webhooks for invoices and payments, and a direct statement connection where your bank offers one.

security.title: Data protection by design
security.body: Each company's data is isolated at the database level, with backups and an audit log.

models.title: How we can work together
models.lead: We adapt the scope to the bank, from a simple code to a deeper integration:
points: A benefit code for business-account clients, with sign-up reporting
A co-branded landing page and materials for branches
A statement connection for automatic payment pairing
A pilot with a limited group of clients before a wider launch

faq.q: Do clients need an account with your bank to use Billanta?
faq.a: No. Billanta works with any bank. A partnership gives your clients a benefit and a smoother start with your account.

faq.q: Does Billanta see clients' banking data?
faq.a: Only what the client connects themselves, and only to pair payments with invoices. Each company's data stays private.

faq.q: How long does a pilot take?
faq.a: A benefit code can run within days. A statement integration depends on the bank's interface; we agree the plan together.

banks.contactBody: Write to us with the contact person and what you have in mind. We prepare a proposal tailored to your bank.

benefits.title: Clients in the EU

benefits.title: Invoice from a voice message
benefits.text: Dictate it to Telegram or WhatsApp. Billanta drafts it, you check it.

event.lead: Czech and Slovak invoicing for freelancers and small businesses. ISDOC, VAT, business registers and VIES on every plan.

benefits.title: Type the company ID, the rest fills in
benefits.text: Client details from Czech and Slovak business registers.

benefits.title: Your accountant gets what they need
benefits.text: ISDOC plus exports for Pohoda and Money S3.

benefits.title: Keeps an eye on limits
benefits.text: Turnover towards VAT registration and a tax calendar with deadlines.

local.headline: Invoice from your phone, right at the job.

benefits.title: Free for occasional invoices

benefits.title: A QR code for your customer
benefits.text: They pay on the spot from their phone, no retyping account numbers.

benefits.title: Nothing to install

benefits.text: Once an invoice is overdue, we remind the customer by e-mail.

benefits.text: A sample company for 24 hours, no e-mail or password.

firstInvoice.seoTitle: Your first invoice: what it must contain and how to issue it
firstInvoice.title: Your first invoice
firstInvoice.lead: What an invoice must contain in Czechia and Slovakia, how to issue one step by step, and which mistakes to avoid. No legal jargon.
firstInvoice.demoCta: Try it on an empty company
firstInvoice.contentTitle: What must be on the invoice
firstInvoice.contentLead: A business that is not a VAT payer needs fewer details than a payer. Billanta checks against your settings that nothing is missing.

cz.title: Czechia
always: Your name or company name, registered address and company ID (IČO)
Your registry entry (a sole trader can state the entry in the trade register)
The customer: name, address and, for a business, its IČO
A unique invoice number from your number series
The issue date and the due date
What you are invoicing, the quantity and the price
The total and how to pay; for a transfer, the account number and variable symbol
vat: Your VAT number (DIČ) and the customer's
The date of the taxable supply (DUZP)
The unit price without VAT and any discount
The tax base, the rate (21 % or 12 %) and the VAT amount in CZK
For reverse charge, a sentence saying the customer accounts for the tax
cz.law: Under § 435 of the Civil Code and § 29 of the VAT Act.

sk.title: Slovakia
always: Your name or business name, registered address and IČO
Your entry in the commercial or trade register, including the entry number
The customer: name, address and, for a business, its IČO
The issue date and the due date
What you are invoicing, the quantity and the price
The total and how to pay; for a transfer, the IBAN and variable symbol
vat: Your VAT number (IČ DPH) and the customer's
The date of supply of the goods or service
The unit price without VAT and any discount
The tax base, the rate (23 %, 19 % or 5 %) and the VAT amount in euros
For reverse charge, the words "prenesenie daňovej povinnosti"
sk.law: Under § 3a of the Commercial Code and § 74 of the VAT Act.

steps.title: Fill in your details
steps.body: Enter your IČO and your company details load from the Czech or Slovak business register. Add your bank account.

steps.title: Add the customer
steps.body: The customer's IČO is enough too. For a private person, enter a name and address.

steps.title: Describe what you invoice
steps.body: The work or goods, the quantity and the price. Be specific: "Logo design, 3 variants" rather than "services".

steps.title: Check the dates
steps.body: The issue date is today, the due date usually 14 days later. A VAT payer adds the supply date and issues within 15 days of it.

steps.title: Issue and send
steps.body: The invoice gets the next number in your series and a QR code for payment. Email it or download the PDF.

steps.title: Watch for the payment
steps.body: Mark it paid when the money arrives, or let bank payments match themselves. After the due date, send a reminder.

vatShown.title: VAT on a non-payer's invoice
vatShown.body: If you are not a VAT payer, leave VAT out. Write it on the invoice and you owe it to the state.

numbering.title: Gaps and duplicate numbers
numbering.body: Numbers should follow on without repeats. Billanta assigns them itself when you issue.

buyer.title: Wrong customer details
buyer.body: A typo in the name or IČO delays payment. Details loaded from the register are exact.

dates.title: Late or wrong dates
dates.body: A VAT payer needs the right supply date and must issue within 15 days of the supply.

editing.title: Rewriting an issued invoice
editing.body: Don't overwrite an issued invoice. Fix a mistake with a credit note and a new invoice.

copies.title: Lost copies
copies.body: Invoices must be kept for years. They stay in the app, and you can set up backups.

ctaBox.title: Try it out first
ctaBox.body: The demo gives you an empty company, and your first invoice takes a few minutes. Nothing is sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I need a Billanta account for my first invoice?
faq.a: No. You can issue a one-off invoice without signing up. An account helps once you want numbered series, payment tracking and everything in one place.

faq.q: Does an invoice need a stamp or a signature?
faq.a: No, the law requires neither. The mandatory details are what count.

faq.q: Can I invoice without an IČO?
faq.a: Invoices are issued by businesses, so you need an IČO. A private person without a trade licence handles occasional income differently.

faq.q: What due date should I set?
faq.a: 14 days is common. Between businesses the law assumes a limit (30 days in Czechia, 60 in Slovakia) unless you explicitly agree otherwise.

faq.q: Is a PDF by email enough?
faq.a: Yes. An electronic invoice is as valid as a paper one if the customer agrees to it, which is normal today.

faq.q: What if I made a mistake on the invoice?
faq.a: While it is a draft, just edit it. An issued invoice is corrected with a credit note, followed by a new invoice.

beginners.seoTitle: Invoicing for beginners: not a VAT payer, first customer
beginners.title: Starting a business? Invoice like this
beginners.lead: The basics for sole traders who are not VAT payers: the first customer, numbering, payments, reminders and when you become a VAT payer.

nonVat.title: Not a VAT payer
nonVat.body: You invoice without VAT and leave VAT off the invoice entirely. Just add a line saying you are not a payer.

firstCustomer.title: The first customer
firstCustomer.body: Agree the price, scope and due date upfront. An email that makes the deal clear is enough.

numbering.title: Numbering
numbering.body: Pick a series, such as year and sequence (2026001). Billanta assigns numbers itself and carries on into the new year.

payment.title: Getting paid
payment.body: Give your account number and variable symbol. The customer scans the QR code in their banking app and types nothing.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.body: When a payment doesn't arrive, Billanta sends the customer a polite reminder after the due date. You choose when.

tax.title: Taxes and contributions
tax.body: Invoices are the basis of your tax return. Work out flat-rate expenses or the flat tax with the calculators below.

beginners.vatTitle: When you become a VAT payer
beginners.vatLead: The threshold counts your turnover over a calendar year. Billanta can show how far from it you are.

cz.title: Czechia
points: The threshold is CZK 2,000,000 of turnover in a calendar year
Cross it and you become a payer from 1 January of the next year
If turnover exceeds CZK 2,536,500, you are a payer from the day after
You can also register voluntarily, for example if you sell mostly to VAT payers

sk.title: Slovakia
points: The threshold is EUR 50,000 of turnover in a calendar year
Cross it and you must apply for registration; you are a payer from the day after it is granted
If turnover exceeds EUR 62,500, you become a payer with the very supply that crossed it
You can also register voluntarily

month.title: Set up your company
month.body: IČO, address, bank account and number series. With the register it takes minutes.

month.title: Issue your first invoice
month.body: Ideally right after the work is done, so the payment isn't delayed.

month.title: Record expenses
month.body: Photograph or upload receipts. They feed your overview and your tax return.

month.title: Check payments
month.body: Connect your bank or mark payments by hand. The overview shows who owes you.

faq.q: Do I have to write that I am not a VAT payer?
faq.a: The law doesn't strictly require it, but it is good practice and saves questions. Billanta adds it for you.

faq.q: Can I make invoices in Excel or Word?
faq.a: You can, but you have to watch numbering, dates and copies yourself. An app does it for you and forgets nothing.

faq.q: What is the Czech flat tax?
faq.a: One monthly payment covering income tax, social and health insurance for Czech sole traders below a certain income. It doesn't suit everyone, so do the maths.

faq.q: Do I need an accountant?
faq.a: Often not at first, especially with flat-rate expenses. When the business grows, invite your accountant to Billanta and they see the records themselves.

faq.q: How much does Billanta cost?
faq.a: Basic invoicing is free. Higher plans add things like bank matching or more users. See pricing for details.

advanced.seoTitle: Invoicing for advanced users: VAT, foreign customers, recurring invoices, API
advanced.title: When invoicing is part of the daily routine
advanced.lead: For VAT payers and growing companies: reverse charge, foreign customers, recurring invoices, payment matching, the API, several companies and team roles.
advanced.topicsTitle: Topics you will meet sooner or later

vat.title: VAT payers
vat.body: Rates, supply dates and the data for your return. Czech VAT returns, control statements and EC sales lists download as XML for EPO.

reverseCharge.title: Reverse charge
reverseCharge.body: For some supplies and for EU VAT payers the customer accounts for the tax. Billanta asks for their VAT number and adds the required wording.

foreign.title: Foreign customers
foreign.body: Invoices in euros or dollars, the exchange rate for the supply date and the conversion for VAT. Invoices can be bilingual too.

recurring.title: Recurring invoices
recurring.body: Invoice rent or a retainer from one template. Each month brings an invoice with the next number in the series.

bank.title: Payment matching
bank.body: Bank payments match by variable symbol and amount. Paid invoices are marked by themselves.

api.title: API and webhooks
api.body: Connect your shop or your own system. Webhooks report when an invoice is paid, viewed or overdue.

companies.title: Several companies
companies.body: One login, separate books. You can hold a different role in each company. Depends on your plan.

roles.title: Team roles
roles.body: An accountant, an assistant or a read-only colleague sees and changes only what they should.

isdoc.title: ISDOC and e-invoices
isdoc.body: Customers' accounting software reads ISDOC invoices by itself, with no retyping.

switch.title: Moving from another app?
switch.body: Bring contacts and issued invoices over from CSV, Fakturoid or BitFaktura. Numbering carries on where you left off.

faq.q: Does Billanta know when to use reverse charge?
faq.a: For a customer with a VAT number from another EU country it offers reverse charge and checks the number in VIES. For domestic cases, such as construction work, you switch it on for the invoice.

faq.q: Can I invoice in a foreign currency?
faq.a: Yes. For Czech companies the ČNB rate for the supply date fills in at issue and can be adjusted by hand. VAT is converted to CZK.

faq.q: Does Billanta handle the Czech control statement?
faq.a: Yes. For Czech VAT payers it prepares the control statement XML with every document, as well as the VAT return and the EC sales list.

faq.q: Is the API in every plan?
faq.a: The API and webhooks are in the paid plans. See pricing for details.

faq.q: Can I manage several companies?
faq.a: Yes, on the top plan. Each company has its own data, number series, bank and team.

roles.seoTitle: Team roles: owner, admin, accountant and read only
roles.title: Team roles
roles.lead: Invite your accountant, an assistant or a colleague. Everyone sees only what they need and changes only what they may. Here is exactly what.

owner.who: Whoever created the company in Billanta
owner.body: Sees and does everything. Answers for the company and is the only one who sets up data backups.
points: All invoicing, expenses, bank and reports
The team, subscription, company settings and API keys
Data backups, and nobody else
The owner's role can't be changed and the owner can't be removed

admin.body: Runs the company on the owner's behalf. May do almost everything except set up data backups.
points: All invoicing, expenses, bank and reports
Invites colleagues and sets their access
Company settings, subscription, API keys, history import
Connects bank accounts

accountant.body: Works with documents and exports, and stays out of company administration.
points: Invoices, contacts, expenses and reports
Syncs the bank but doesn't connect new accounts
Bookkeeping exports up front
Doesn't see the team, subscription or API keys

viewer.body: Looks, changes nothing. Suits anyone who needs the overview.
points: Reads invoices, contacts, expenses, bank and reports
Can't issue, edit or delete anything
Doesn't see company settings

roles.tableLead: The default access of each role. For the accountant and read-only roles, the owner or an admin can adjust access area by area.
roles.tableNote: The accountant syncs the bank; new accounts are connected by the owner or an admin. Accountants can switch on the due-date calendar in integrations themselves. Anyone can leave a company or create their own.
roles.presetsLead: Pick a profile when you invite someone and access is set for you. You can adjust it at any time.

invoicer.title: Invoicer
invoicer.body: Issues invoices and manages contacts, reads the bank. No access to expenses or reports.

expenses.title: Expenses assistant
expenses.body: Records expenses and receipts, reads invoices and contacts.

auditor.title: Tax advisor / auditor
auditor.body: Reads everything, changes nothing. Ideal for a review or the year-end close.

viewer.title: Read only
viewer.body: Sees invoices, contacts and expenses. Not the bank or reports.

roles.demoTitle: See it through each role's eyes
roles.demoLead: Open the demo as the owner, the accountant or a read-only colleague. The overview, menu and settings show only what that role can do.

faq.q: How many people can I invite?
faq.a: It depends on your plan, from a single user to a whole team. See pricing for details.

faq.q: Does my accountant pay for an account?
faq.a: No. You invite them by email and they sign in with their own account, which can serve several clients.

faq.q: What does a member see on a page they can't use?
faq.a: The menu and overview only offer what they can do. If they open a hidden page from a link, they see a note that they have no access to it.

faq.q: Can I find out who changed what?
faq.a: Yes. The change history shows the author, the time, and the old and new value of each change.

faq.q: Can one person hold different roles in different companies?
faq.a: Yes. For example, owner of their own company and accountant at a client's.

owners.seoTitle: Billanta for business owners: overview, team and control
owners.title: For business owners
owners.lead: You create the company in Billanta and you have the final say. You see everything, invite your team and decide who may do what.
owners.cardsTitle: What you get as the owner

overview.title: The full overview
overview.body: Who owes you, what is overdue, turnover and expenses. All on one screen, on your phone too.

team.title: Your team in check
team.body: In Settings → Team, invite your accountant or an assistant and adjust their access area by area.

audit.title: Change history
audit.body: For every invoice you see who changed it, when and why. Even when it was AI or the API.

billing.title: Subscription and settings
billing.body: You, or an admin, manage the plan, company details, number series and API keys.

backups.title: Backups only through you
backups.body: Only the owner sets where and how often the company's data is backed up. Nobody else can redirect it.

companies.title: Several companies
companies.body: Add another company under the same login. Data and teams stay separate. Depends on your plan.

steps.title: Invite your accountant
steps.body: Enter their email and the Accountant role. They take exports and records themselves, so you send nothing.

steps.title: Invite an assistant
steps.body: Give an office manager the Admin role. Someone who only invoices gets the Invoicer profile.

steps.title: Adjust access
steps.body: For the accountant and read-only roles, switch single areas on or off, such as the bank or reports.

steps.title: Check the history
steps.body: Activity shows who changed what. An issued invoice can only be corrected with a stated reason.

faq.q: Can someone on the team remove me?
faq.a: No. The owner can't be removed from the company and the owner's role can't be changed.

faq.q: Why does only the owner set up backups?
faq.a: A backup holds all of the company's data, so only the person who answers for the company decides where it goes.

faq.q: What if my accountant leaves?
faq.a: Remove them in Settings → Team and their access ends at once. The data stays with the company.

faq.q: Can I see the company the way my accountant does?
faq.a: In the demo, yes: open it in the accountant or read-only view.

assistants.seoTitle: Billanta for assistants and office managers
assistants.title: For assistants and office managers
assistants.lead: Handling invoices and paperwork for someone else? Billanta gives you access that fits: the whole company, or just invoices or expenses.

admin.title: Admin
admin.body: You run the company for the owner: invoices, expenses, bank, team and settings. Only data backups stay with the owner.

invoicer.title: Invoicer
invoicer.body: You issue invoices and keep contacts. You see bank payments, but not expenses or reports.

expenses.title: Expenses assistant
expenses.body: You record expenses and receipts. You see invoices and contacts but don't change them.

contacts.title: Contacts from the register
contacts.body: Add a new customer by IČO and the details load from the business register. No retyping.

tailored.title: An app that fits your role
tailored.body: The overview, menu, search and mobile navigation show only the actions you may take.

limits.title: Clear limits
limits.body: Settings you can't use show a note that admins manage them. You can't break anything.

steps.title: Accept the invitation
steps.body: The owner invites you by email. Sign in with your account or create one on the spot.

steps.title: Look around the overview
steps.body: The home screen shows only what you have access to: drafts, due dates or expenses.

steps.title: Issue or record
steps.body: An invoicer issues an invoice, an expenses assistant uploads a receipt. Everything goes into the change history.

steps.title: Need more?
steps.body: Ask the owner or an admin to widen your access. The change applies at once.

faq.q: What is the difference between an admin and the owner?
faq.a: An admin may do almost everything the owner can, but doesn't set up data backups and can't remove the owner or change the owner's role.

faq.q: Can I work for several companies?
faq.a: Yes. One login can belong to several companies, with a different role in each.

faq.q: As an invoicer, will I see expenses or profit?
faq.a: No. The Invoicer profile has no access to expenses or reports.

faq.q: What if I leave the company?
faq.a: You can leave a company yourself at any time. The invoices you issued stay with the company.

taxReturn.noTenant: Fill in your company's billing details first.

taxReturn.basisAccrual: Accounting: income by the date of supply.

taxReturn.vatPayerNo: You are not VAT-registered, amounts are gross.

taxReturn.legalEntitySk: A company files the corporate income tax return (DPPO). Flat-rate expenses don't apply, and the accounts decide the profit – use these sums as a cross-check.
taxReturn.flatLead: Under § 7 (7) of the Czech Income Tax Act you can claim a share of income instead of actual expenses. The rate depends on the activity, each with a yearly cap.
taxReturn.flatLeadSk: In Slovakia there is one flat rate (§ 6 (10) ZDP) with a yearly cap; the insurance paid is deducted on top.

rates.40: 40 % – liberal professions and other business under special laws, copyright income.
rates.60: 60 % – other trades (most unqualified, qualified and licensed trades).
rates.80: 80 % – crafts trades, agriculture, forestry and water management.

better.equal: The {rate} % flat rate and actual expenses come out the same.

taxReturn.estimateLeadSk: Income tax after the basic personal allowance, and insurance for the year at this year's rates.
taxReturn.skInsuranceNote: The insurance paid is taken from the advances in Settings → Billing details and lowers the tax base in both options.
taxReturn.noParams: Rates and limits for {year} aren't published yet, so there is no tax estimate. The sums and deadlines apply.
taxReturn.flatTaxLead: One monthly payment covering income tax, social and health insurance (§ 2a ZDP). For non-VAT payers with income up to CZK 2 million; you join by notifying by 10 January.
taxReturn.flatTaxBand: With this income you would be in band {band}: {total} for the year.

flatTaxNo.vat_payer: A VAT payer cannot use the flat tax.
flatTaxNo.over_limit: The flat tax isn't available with this income (limit CZK 2 million, less at the lower flat rates).
flatTaxNo.no_data: The flat tax amounts for this year are missing.

best.flat_tax: By this estimate, the flat tax is the cheapest.
best.flat_expenses: By this estimate, the regular regime with flat-rate expenses is the cheapest.
best.actual_expenses: By this estimate, the regular regime with actual expenses is the cheapest.

taxReturn.inFlatTaxRegime: Your settings say you are in the flat-tax regime. If you didn't leave it during the year or exceed the limit, you usually file neither the return nor the insurance statements.
taxReturn.flatTaxCalculator: Full comparison in the flat tax calculator

CZ.advisor: Through a tax advisor (power of attorney filed by the first deadline)

diff.flatSk: One flat rate of {rate} %, at most {cap} a year.
diff.deadlineCz: {paper} on paper, {electronic} electronically, {advisor} through a tax advisor.
diff.deadlineSk: {paper}; after notifying the tax office, {extended} (up to 6 months with foreign income).
diff.insuranceCz: A sole trader's own insurance is not a tax expense (§ 25 ZDP).
diff.insuranceSk: The insurance paid is deducted from the tax base, on top of the flat rate too.
diff.flatTaxCz: Yes, for non-VAT payers with income up to CZK 2 million.
diff.flatTaxSk: No. A reduced 15 % income tax rate applies at lower income.
diff.formCz: The personal income tax return, then within a month the statements for ČSSZ and the health insurer.
diff.formSk: Tax return type B; the Social Insurance Agency takes the income from the tax office.

taxReturn.noteInsuranceSk: Social and health insurance paid is deducted from the tax base next to both the flat rate and actual expenses (§ 6 (10) and (11) ZDP).
taxReturn.noteEstimate: The estimate uses only the basic taxpayer credit, without other credits, deductions or other income (employment, rent).
taxReturn.noteEstimateSk: The estimate uses only the basic personal allowance, without other deductions, the child bonus or other income.

landing.ctaTitle: A summary from your own invoices
landing.ctaBody: When you invoice in Billanta, the basis for your return is ready without retyping anything. Just add what isn't in the app.

faq.q: Is this tax advice?
faq.a: No. It sums up your own documents with a rough calculation at the statutory rates. Check the figures before filing, with an accountant or tax advisor if needed.

faq.q: When are flat-rate expenses better than actual expenses?
faq.a: When your actual expenses are lower than the share of income your activity allows. The summary shows both numbers side by side, with the yearly cap.

faq.q: Is it free?
faq.a: Yes, on every plan including the free one, for Czech and Slovak sole traders alike.

faq.q: What if I invoice in another currency?
faq.a: Foreign-currency invoices are converted at the rate stored with the document. Documents without a rate are listed separately so nothing gets lost.

landing.disclaimer: Rates, caps and deadlines follow the Czech and Slovak income tax acts and tax procedure codes for the given year. The information is indicative and does not replace a tax advisor.

switchBanner.title: Switching from another app? Import your data in minutes
switchBanner.text: Bring over contacts, issued invoices and your number sequence from a Fakturoid, iDoklad, SuperFaktura or other export.

switchPage.seoTitle: Switch to Billanta from another invoicing app
switchPage.title: Switch to Billanta and take your data with you
switchPage.lead: Bring over contacts, issued invoices and your number sequence from the export your current app gives you. The import recognises where the file comes from and shows a preview before anything is saved.
switchPage.otherText: The import reads your own spreadsheet too. Any column it does not recognise you match in the preview.
how: Download an export of invoices and contacts from your old app as CSV or Excel.
Upload the file to Billanta. We recognise which app it comes from and match the columns.
Check invoices, customers and numbering in the preview. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
switchPage.exportTitle: How to get your data out
transfers: Customers with company ID, tax ID and address. Ones you already have in Billanta are matched, not duplicated.
Issued invoices with dates, amounts, currency and payment status. Nothing is sent again and no reminders go out.
Your number sequence: the next invoice follows the last imported one and, if you like, we adopt the number format too.
Invoice line items when the export includes them; otherwise one line for the full amount.
switchPage.note: We describe the steps in general terms; button names can differ between versions of the app.
switchPage.ctaTitle: Create a free account and upload your export
switchPage.ctaLead: After signing up we take you straight to the import. Nothing changes in your old app.
switchPage.haveAccount: Already have an account? Open the import

faq.q: Will I lose anything in my old app?
faq.a: No. The import only reads the file you download. Nothing changes in the old app and you can keep using it until you are sure.

faq.q: What if the import does not recognise some columns?
faq.a: In the preview you pick what each column contains and check the file again. Nothing is saved without your confirmation.

faq.q: Will invoice numbering continue?
faq.a: Yes. The next invoice gets the number after the highest imported one. If your old app used a different number format, the preview offers to adopt it.

faq.q: Do I need to convert an Excel file to CSV?
faq.a: No, upload the .xlsx file directly. Only the old .xls format needs to be saved again as .xlsx in Excel.

fakturoid.title: Switching from Fakturoid to Billanta
fakturoid.lead: There are two ways to leave Fakturoid: a direct API connection or a CSV export. Both end in a preview where you check everything.
steps: Your Fakturoid user account settings give you API v3 access (Client ID and Client secret).
Enter them in the Billanta import and we load invoices, proformas, credit notes and the address book at once.
Without the API, export the invoice and contact lists to CSV; upload the contacts first.
fakturoid.extra: With the API connection we also bring over proforma invoices, credit notes, payments and the original PDFs.
fakturoid.seoTitle: Switching from Fakturoid to Billanta – export and import guide

idoklad.title: Switching from iDoklad to Billanta
idoklad.lead: From iDoklad, export the list of issued invoices and your contacts. You upload the Excel file directly, no conversion needed.
steps: In the list of issued invoices, select the documents to move.
Use the export to Excel or CSV.
Export contacts the same way and upload them to Billanta first.
idoklad.extra: We work out the VAT rate from the amounts even when the export has no separate column for it.
idoklad.seoTitle: Switching from iDoklad to Billanta – export and import guide

superfaktura.title: Switching from SuperFaktura to Billanta
superfaktura.lead: From SuperFaktura, download the invoice overview and client directory. The import reads both Czech and Slovak exports, including invoices in euro.
steps: In the invoice overview, filter the period you want to move.
Download the list as Excel or CSV.
Export clients the same way and upload them to Billanta first.
superfaktura.extra: A Slovak VAT ID (IČ DPH) stays with the customer, separate from the tax ID (DIČ).
superfaktura.seoTitle: Switching from SuperFaktura to Billanta – export and import guide

vyfakturuj.title: Switching from Vyfakturuj to Billanta
vyfakturuj.lead: From Vyfakturuj you bring over issued invoices including their line items. An export of documents and contacts is all it takes.
steps: In the document list, filter issued invoices for the period you want to move.
Download them as CSV or Excel, ideally with line items.
Export contacts separately and upload them to Billanta first.
vyfakturuj.extra: An export with line items comes over line by line, with quantity, price and VAT rate.
vyfakturuj.seoTitle: Switching from Vyfakturuj to Billanta – export and import guide

kros.title: Switching from KROS Fakturácia to Billanta
kros.lead: From KROS Fakturácia, export issued invoices and partners to Excel. The import reads Slovak column names and invoices in euro.
steps: In the list of issued invoices, select the documents to move.
Export the list to Excel or CSV.
Export partners the same way and upload them to Billanta first.
kros.extra: The Slovak VAT ID (IČ DPH) stays separate from the tax ID (DIČ), and we work out the VAT rate from the amounts.
kros.seoTitle: Switching from KROS Fakturácia to Billanta – export and import guide

billdu.title: Switching from Billdu to Billanta
billdu.lead: From Billdu, download the document export in the web app. The import understands English column names too.
steps: In the Billdu web app, open the invoice list and find the document export.
Choose CSV or Excel and the period you want to move.
Export clients separately and upload them to Billanta first.
billdu.extra: Payment status and dates in YYYY-MM-DD format are converted for you.
billdu.seoTitle: Switching from Billdu to Billanta – export and import guide

bitfaktura.title: Switching from BitFaktura to Billanta
bitfaktura.lead: You can leave BitFaktura with an API code or with a CSV export of invoices. A sequence like 1/09/2025 carries on.
steps: The integrations in your BitFaktura account settings show an API authorisation code.
Enter it in the Billanta import with your account name and we load invoices and the whole address book.
Without the code, export invoices to CSV and upload the file in the import.
bitfaktura.extra: With the API code we also load contacts you have not invoiced yet, exchange rates and payment methods.
bitfaktura.seoTitle: Switching from BitFaktura to Billanta – export and import guide

invoiceTemplates.indexTitle: Czech invoice templates – for VAT payers and non-payers
invoiceTemplates.indexDescription: Invoice templates under Czech law: non-VAT payer and VAT payer invoices, proforma, credit note, domestic reverse charge and identified person. Each with the required details and a free online editor.
invoiceTemplates.indexLead: Pick your situation to see a filled-in sample, the required details with links to the law, and a button that opens the editor preset for that document. The PDF is free, no sign-up needed.
how: Check the sample to see what belongs on the invoice and where.
Open the editor with the document type already set and add your own details.
Download the finished PDF with a QR payment code. Nothing is stored, no account needed.

common.fieldsLead: Each item links to the section of Czech law that requires it (in Czech).
common.useNote: The editor opens with the document type set. The PDF is free, no sign-up needed.
common.rulesNote: These templates follow Czech law. For special cases (foreign customers, exempt supplies) check the details in the law or with a tax adviser.

laws.NVUO: of Slovak Government Regulation No. 21/2013 Coll.

contractor.name: Stavby Kučera s.r.o.
ids: File C 98765, Regional Court in Brno

nonPayer.name: Non-VAT payer
nonPayer.title: Invoice template for non-VAT payers (Czech Republic)
nonPayer.description: Czech invoice template for non-VAT payers: a filled-in sample, the details required by the Civil Code and the Accounting Act, and a free online editor with PDF.
nonPayer.lead: The most common invoice of a Czech freelancer. A non-payer shows no VAT and no date of taxable supply, but must say who issued the invoice, to whom and for what.
notes: Sole trader registered in the Trade Register.

lines.d: Product photography for an online shop (40 shots)

when: You are not registered for VAT (turnover up to CZK 2,000,000 in a calendar year) and invoice a customer in the Czech Republic.
This applies to sole traders and companies that are not VAT payers. For services to businesses in another EU country you usually become an identified person – see the separate template.

fields.name: Supplier's name, registered address and company ID (IČO)
fields.text: A business shows them on every business document, invoices included.

fields.name: Entry in a public register
fields.text: Only if you are in one: a company shows the court and file number. A sole trader only in the Trade Register does not have to.

fields.name: Customer
fields.text: Name and address, plus the company ID for a business, so it is clear who the parties are.

fields.name: Document number
fields.text: A unique number for the invoice, ideally from an ascending series.

fields.name: What was supplied and the amount
fields.text: What you delivered, how much and for what price. The total amount due.

fields.name: Issue date
fields.text: When the document was made.

fields.name: A note that you are not a VAT payer
fields.text: Not strictly required, but it saves questions about why there is no VAT.

pitfalls: Do not show a "CZ…" VAT ID if you are neither a payer nor an identified person – the customer could expect a tax document.
A due date and bank account are not legally required, but without them you get paid later.

vatPayer.name: VAT payer
vatPayer.title: Invoice template for VAT payers (Czech tax document)
vatPayer.description: Czech VAT invoice template: a tax document with VAT IDs, date of taxable supply and VAT summary. Required details under Section 29 of the VAT Act and a free online editor.
vatPayer.lead: A VAT payer's invoice is a tax document. On top of the usual details it must show both VAT IDs, the date of taxable supply, the tax base, the rate and the VAT amount.
notes: Sole trader registered in the Trade Register.
when: You are a Czech VAT payer supplying goods or services in the Czech Republic, where you account for the VAT.
Issue the tax document within 15 days of the taxable supply or of receiving payment.

fields.name: Supplier and its VAT ID
fields.text: Name, registered address and tax identification number (DIČ).

fields.name: Customer and its VAT ID
fields.text: If the customer is a VAT payer, its VAT ID is shown too.

fields.name: Document number
fields.text: Unique within one or more series.

fields.name: Scope and subject of the supply
fields.text: What and how much you supplied.

fields.name: Issue date and date of taxable supply
fields.text: The date of taxable supply is required when it differs from the issue date – in practice, always show it.

fields.name: Unit price without VAT and discount
fields.text: Unit price excluding VAT and any discount not already in it.

fields.name: Tax base, rate and VAT amount
fields.text: Per rate; the VAT amount in CZK even on a foreign-currency invoice.

fields.name: Civil Code details
fields.text: Registered address, company ID and any public register entry.

pitfalls: On a EUR invoice, show the VAT in CZK as well, with the exchange rate used.
The due date is not a required detail of a tax document, but without it a debt is hard to chase.

proforma.name: Proforma invoice
proforma.title: Proforma invoice template (Czech zálohová faktura)
proforma.description: Czech proforma invoice template: what to put on it, why it is not a tax document and which document to issue once paid. Free online editor and PDF.
proforma.lead: A proforma invoice asks for payment in advance. It is not a tax document, so the customer cannot deduct VAT from it. Once paid, a VAT payer issues a tax document.
notes: This proforma invoice is not a tax document.
We will send a tax document for the payment once it reaches our account.
when: You want payment up front before starting work or shipping goods.
Once paid, a VAT payer usually issues a tax document for the payment and deducts the advance on the final invoice. A non-payer just deducts it on the final invoice.

fields.name: Supplier and customer
fields.text: Name, registered address and company ID; it is a business document.

fields.name: Proforma number
fields.text: Use a separate series so it is not mixed up with tax documents.

fields.name: Advance amount and due date
fields.text: How much and by when, and the bank account.

fields.name: A note that it is not a tax document
fields.text: Recommended: it tells the customer they cannot claim VAT from it.

fields.name: Tax document after payment
fields.text: Receiving an advance payment usually makes the VAT due; the payer issues a tax document for it.

pitfalls: Do not show a date of taxable supply on a proforma – it only arises when the payment is received.
Remember to deduct the advance on the final invoice, or the customer pays twice.

creditNote.name: Credit note
creditNote.title: Credit note template (Czech corrective tax document)
creditNote.description: Czech credit note template: a reference to the original invoice, the reason for the correction and the difference in base and VAT. Required details under Section 46 of the VAT Act.
creditNote.lead: When you lower the price after invoicing (discount, complaint, returned goods) or raise it, you issue a corrective tax document. It corrects the original invoice, it does not replace it.
creditNote.reason: Price discount after a complaint about the logo design
when: A discount given after invoicing, an accepted complaint, returned goods or a cancelled part of the supply.
The original invoice stays valid; the credit note records only the difference.

fields.name: Both parties and their VAT IDs
fields.text: Same as on an ordinary tax document.

fields.name: Credit note number
fields.text: Its own number from your series.

fields.name: Original document number
fields.text: The invoice you are correcting.

fields.name: Reason for the correction
fields.text: Short and specific, e.g. a discount after a complaint.

fields.name: Difference in base and VAT
fields.text: The difference between the corrected and the original base and VAT, negative for a reduction.

fields.name: Correcting the tax base
fields.text: When and under what conditions the correction is made.

pitfalls: A non-VAT payer does not issue a corrective tax document – a plain credit note as an accounting document, referring to the original invoice, is enough.
Do not cancel or overwrite the original invoice; it stays in your records.

reverseCharge.name: Reverse charge
reverseCharge.title: Domestic reverse charge invoice template (Czech Republic)
reverseCharge.description: Czech domestic reverse charge invoice template (Section 92a of the VAT Act), e.g. for construction work: the "daň odvede zákazník" note, the customer's VAT ID and the amount without VAT.
reverseCharge.lead: For construction and assembly work, waste, metals and other supplies under Section 92a of the Czech VAT Act, the customer accounts for the VAT. The supplier invoices without VAT and adds "daň odvede zákazník" (the customer will pay the tax).
notes: Reverse charge under Section 92e of the VAT Act (construction and assembly work).

lines.d: Wall and floor tiling, materials included

when: Both of you are Czech VAT payers and the supply is one the regime covers (Sections 92b to 92e and the government decree).
Most often construction and assembly work (CZ-CPA 41 to 43), supplies of waste and scrap, or emission allowances.

fields.name: The note "daň odvede zákazník"
fields.text: A required statement on the tax document when the customer accounts for the VAT.

fields.name: Supplier's and customer's VAT IDs
fields.text: The regime applies only between VAT payers, so the customer's VAT ID is essential.

fields.name: Tax base without VAT
fields.text: You do not show the VAT amount; the customer calculates and declares it. Showing the rate helps them.

fields.name: Other tax document details
fields.text: Number, dates, subject and scope of the supply, unit price.

fields.name: Control statement
fields.text: The supplier reports the supply in section A.1 of the control statement, the customer in section B.1.

pitfalls: If the customer is not a VAT payer (e.g. a private person), the regime does not apply and you charge VAT.
Before sending, check in the VAT payer register that the customer really is a payer.

identified.name: Identified person
identified.title: Invoice template for an identified person (services to the EU)
identified.description: Czech invoice template for an identified person billing a business in another EU country: both VAT IDs, no VAT, the "daň odvede zákazník" note. Required details and a free online editor.
identified.lead: A Czech non-VAT payer who supplies a service to a business in another EU country becomes an identified person. They invoice without Czech VAT, show their own and the customer's VAT IDs and state that the customer accounts for the tax.

lines.d: Web design – online shop theme update, October 2026

when: You are not a VAT payer and supply a service (programming, design, marketing) to a business registered for VAT in another EU country.
Register as an identified person within 15 days of the supply; you do not become a VAT payer.

fields.name: Supplier's VAT ID
fields.text: An identified person gets a CZ… VAT ID and shows it on the invoice.

fields.name: Customer's VAT ID from another country
fields.text: Check it in VIES; without a valid VAT ID there is no reverse charge.

fields.name: The note "daň odvede zákazník"
fields.text: The customer declares the VAT in their country; the invoice shows the amount without VAT.

fields.name: Date of the supply
fields.text: The day the service was supplied; it decides when you report it.

fields.name: EC Sales List
fields.text: File the EC Sales List (souhrnné hlášení) for the month you supplied the service.

pitfalls: If you invoice a private person in the EU, you do not become an identified person; it is an ordinary non-payer invoice.
For services you buy from foreign companies (Facebook or Google ads) you account for Czech VAT yourself – the other side of the same obligation.

requirementsLink.title: What must an invoice contain?
requirementsLink.text: Tell us who you are and what you issue, and we list the required items for exactly your case.

paymentReminders.indexTitle: Free payment reminder and demand letter templates
paymentReminders.indexDescription: Payment reminder, demand for payment and pre-action notice templates under Czech law. Fill in the debtor and amount, pick a tone, then copy the text or download a PDF.
paymentReminders.indexLead: Three letters for an overdue invoice, from a friendly reminder to a notice before legal action. The generator below fills them in for you – copy the text into an email or download a PDF. No sign-up.
paymentReminders.howTitle: What to do about an unpaid invoice
how: A few days after the due date, send a polite reminder. Often it was simply overlooked.
If the payment still doesn't arrive, send a demand for payment with a new deadline and a note on late-payment interest.
Before you sue, send a pre-action notice at least 7 days in advance. Without it the court may not award you your legal costs.
Keep every letter together with proof that you sent it.

common.fieldsLead: Where the law sets a requirement, the item links to the provision.
common.rulesNote: These templates follow Czech law and are not legal advice. For large or disputed claims, talk to a lawyer.

auto.title: Let Billanta send the reminders for you
auto.text: When an invoice issued in Billanta goes overdue, your customer automatically gets a polite email reminder with a link to the invoice and its QR payment. You set the interval and the maximum number of reminders, and they stop as soon as the invoice is paid.

fromInvoices.title: Invoice overdue? Payment reminder templates
fromInvoices.text: A reminder, a demand for payment and a pre-action notice. Fill them in online, then copy them or download a PDF.

reminder.name: Payment reminder
reminder.title: Payment reminder template for an unpaid invoice
reminder.description: A polite or firm reminder for an overdue invoice. Fill in the details, then copy the text into an email or download a free PDF.
reminder.lead: The first letter after the due date: it points to the invoice and sets a new deadline.
when: Send a reminder a few days after the due date, typically 3 to 7 days. The customer is in default from the day after the due date, but the first letter is mainly a nudge that the invoice exists.
The law prescribes no form for a reminder. An email is enough unless your contract says otherwise.

fields.name: Invoice number, amount and due date
fields.text: So the customer can find and match the payment easily.

fields.name: A note that the debtor is in default
fields.text: Whoever doesn't pay on time is in default. In the first reminder a factual mention is enough.

fields.name: New deadline and payment details
fields.text: A specific date and the account number, ideally with the invoice number as the payment reference.

fields.name: A request to get in touch if already paid
fields.text: Payments and reminders cross in the post. A polite line avoids a pointless argument.

pitfalls: Check your bank statement before sending. A reminder for a paid invoice hurts the relationship.
Keep it factual and free of threats. The firmer tone belongs in the demand for payment.
A reminder doesn't extend anything: late-payment interest runs from the day after the due date, whatever the new deadline.

demand.name: Demand for payment
demand.title: Demand for payment template with late-payment interest
demand.description: A demand for payment citing statutory late-payment interest and the CZK 1,200 recovery costs. Fill it in online, then copy it or download a PDF.
demand.lead: The second letter: firmer, with late-payment interest and the costs of recovering the debt.
when: Send a demand for payment when the reminder didn't work, usually 2 to 4 weeks after the due date.
It tells the debtor that on top of the amount owed they may owe late-payment interest and, between businesses, the costs of recovering the debt.

fields.name: Amount owed and the invoice
fields.text: Invoice number, amount and the due date after which the debtor is in default.

fields.name: Late-payment interest
fields.text: The creditor can claim statutory late-payment interest. The annual rate is the Czech National Bank repo rate valid on the first day of the calendar half-year in which the default began, plus 8 percentage points.

fields.name: Costs of recovering the debt
fields.text: At least CZK 1,200 per claim. Only claim them from businesses.

fields.name: New deadline and payment details
fields.text: A specific date by which the payment must arrive, and where to send it.

pitfalls: Count interest from the day after the due date, not from the date of the reminder.
If your contract sets its own interest rate or a contractual penalty, refer to the contract instead of the statutory rate.
Don't claim the CZK 1,200 from consumers.

preAction.name: Pre-action notice
preAction.title: Pre-action notice template for an unpaid invoice
preAction.description: A pre-action notice (demand for performance under § 142a of the Czech Civil Procedure Code). Send it at least 7 days before suing, or you may not recover your legal costs.
preAction.lead: The last letter before going to court: without it you may not get your legal costs back.
when: Send a pre-action notice once you've decided to take the debt to court.
A claimant who wins is entitled to their legal costs only if they sent the defendant a demand for performance at least 7 days before filing, to their delivery address, residence or registered office.

fields.name: An explicit demand for performance
fields.text: The letter must make clear exactly what the debtor has to pay and by when.

fields.name: Debtor's address
fields.text: The delivery address, residence or registered office. Check it in the commercial register or ARES.

fields.name: Notice of legal action
fields.text: That if the deadline passes without payment you will sue and claim your legal costs.

fields.name: Late-payment interest and costs
fields.text: Add the statutory late-payment interest to the amount owed and, between businesses, the costs of recovering the debt.

pitfalls: At least 7 days must pass between sending the notice and filing the claim.
Send it by registered post or to the debtor's data box and keep proof of sending. You will need it in court.
A notice sent only by email is harder to prove.

Please pay {pay} by {deadline} at the latest, using the invoice number as the payment reference.
If you have already paid, please disregard this reminder. Thank you.
invoice no. {invoice} for {amount} was due on {due} and remains unpaid. You have been in default since {dayAfter}.
We ask you to pay {pay} by {deadline} at the latest.
If the payment doesn't arrive by then, we will also claim statutory late-payment interest.
despite our reminder, we still haven't received payment of invoice no. {invoice} for {amount}, due on {due}.
We therefore ask you to pay {pay} by {deadline} at the latest.
Please note that you have been in default since {dayAfter} and that, on top of the amount owed, we may claim statutory late-payment interest.
If you are having trouble paying, please get in touch. We are happy to agree on a solution.
we demand payment of invoice no. {invoice} for {amount}, which was due on {due}. You have been in default since {dayAfter}.
Pay the amount owed {pay} by {deadline} at the latest.
On top of the amount owed, we claim statutory late-payment interest at the Czech National Bank repo rate plus 8 percentage points and CZK 1,200 as the costs of recovering the debt.
If the payment doesn't arrive by then, we will pass the debt on for collection.
we hereby demand performance under § 142a of the Czech Civil Procedure Code.
You have not yet paid invoice no. {invoice} for {amount}, due on {due}. You have been in default since {dayAfter}.
Pay the amount owed {pay} by {deadline} at the latest, together with statutory late-payment interest.
If the payment doesn't arrive by then, we will file a claim and seek our legal costs as well. We would rather avoid that, so please get in touch if you are having trouble paying.
we hereby demand performance under § 142a of the Czech Civil Procedure Code.
You have not paid invoice no. {invoice} for {amount}, due on {due}, despite our earlier reminders. You have been in default since {dayAfter}.
Pay the amount owed {pay} by {deadline} at the latest, together with statutory late-payment interest and CZK 1,200 as the costs of recovering the debt.
If the payment doesn't arrive by then, we will file a claim without further notice and seek our legal costs as well.

schoolLessons.indexMetaTitle: Invoicing lessons for schools and colleges – ready lessons with worksheets
schoolLessons.indexLead: 45-minute lessons on Czech invoicing and VAT at three levels: from financial literacy in lower secondary school to VAT returns and working with an accountant at college. Goals, teacher notes, a task in the no-signup demo and a worksheet with answers. Free, for print or the projector.
schoolLessons.indexMeta: Ready-to-teach 45-minute lessons on Czech invoicing and VAT for lower and upper secondary schools, colleges and courses: what an invoice is, invoice details, tax point, VAT rates, credit notes, advances, reminders, VAT returns, the control statement and bank matching. Worksheets with answers.
how: Each lesson has goals, a lesson plan, an explanation of the key terms with links to the exact provisions, and notes for the teacher.
Students work through a step-by-step task in the Billanta demo. The demo needs no signup or e-mail, and every student gets their own company with sample data.
Print the worksheet in the student version (without answers). The answers and the print with answers appear once you sign in with a teacher account.
schoolLessons.rvpNote: The lower secondary lessons fit financial literacy, and the upper secondary ones the economics and accounting content of the Czech framework curricula (RVP) for business academies. How they map to years and subjects is up to the school.
schoolLessons.lawBasis: The lessons follow Czech law. Links to the legislation lead to the Czech texts.
schoolLessons.lawNote: Links lead to the current consolidated Czech texts on zakonyprolidi.cz.

schoolLessons.checked: We last checked the legal references on {date}. Laws change, so check the current wording before the lesson. The lessons are for teaching and are not tax advice.
